pages.text:
[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

Consistency makes guides easier to read and maintain. This guide covers formatting, structure, and PvME-specific conventions.

​

Sections & Templates

⬥ We have various types of guides, each of which has a unique structure and sections within

⬥ Most templates you will require can be found on the [https://pvme.io/guide-editor/ Guide Editor]:

[https://img.pvme.io/images/By04eu9tkH.png Guide illustration] ​

Language & Formatting

⬥ Use UK English (e.g. armour, not armour; defence, not defense)

⬥ Date format: 22nd July 2013

⬥ Do not end lines with blank space (this is referred to as "trailing whitespace")

​

Styling & Punctuation

Always end full sentences with a full stop / period

⬥ Exceptions:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• bullet points should not end in a full stop

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Any sentence ending in an emoji should not end in a full stop 🚀

​

⬥ Text styles:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• **Bold** ‎– Key items or emphases

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• *Italic* ‎– Inline notes or footnotes

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• __Underline__ ‎– Optional emphasis

​

Emojis

⬥ Spacing: Emojis require a space before and after:

❌ Detonate<:deto:123> is a spell.
❌ Spellbook Swap <:SBS:543875425055670275>is a spell.
✅ Spellbook Swap <:SBS:543875425055670275> is a spell.

​

⬥ There are a few exceptions where spaces are not needed:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Letter prefixes (r, s, _)

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Punctuation/backslash/backtick prefixes

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Trailing punctuation or underscore

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Inside backticks (embeds)

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Invisible characters

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Allowed examples:

r<:emoji:1> <:emoji:7>. "… <:emoji:4> …" <:emoji:7>! `…<:emoji:11>…` <emoji:73>\n\u00a0

​

Notes

⬥ Use sparingly to highlight key info

⬥ Put notes below their related content

⬥ For a single note, show it in-line and italic:

*Note: This is a note.*

⬥ For multiple notes, show as bullets and italic:

*Notes:*
⬥ *This is a note*
⬥ *This is another note*

​

Headings

⬥ Headings represent sections and sub-sections

​

⬥ Always put a . ‎on the line before any heading (ignore the backslash \ ‎in the below example)

<End of previous section>

\.
## __Section 2__
This is the new section

​

⬥ Use # ‎and underline the title

⬥ Use ## ‎/ ### ‎and underline level 1 and 2 headings

⬥ Level 3 headings:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Discord doesn't allow #### ‎for level 3 headings

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Therefore remove the underline to distinguish

​

# Title
## __Section 1__
### __Sub-section 1.1__
### Sub-sub-section 1.1.1

## __Section 2__

## __Section 3__
### __Sub-section 3.1__

​

⬥ Headings should be capitalised following the Oxford style:

✅ Capitalise
⬥ First and last word ⬥ Nouns ⬥ Pronouns ⬥ Verbs ⬥ Adjectives ⬥ Adverbs ⬥ Any word over four letters
❌ Don’t capitalise
⬥ Articles (a, an, the) ⬥ Prepositions (to, on, in, for, with, etc.) ⬥ Conjunctions (and, but, or, nor, etc.)

​

Lists

⬥ Bulleted lists use different characters depending on the level

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Level 2 bullets should be indented 4 spaces

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ Level 3 bullets should be indented 8 spaces

​

1) Numbered Lists follow the same rules with indentation

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎a) Level 2 should use letters

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ Level 3 should be bullets

​

⬥ Where visually dense, you may add line breaks between list items (like above this bullet)

​

Links and Embedded Content

⬥ Only use content from https://runescape.wiki/, https://www.youtube.com/ ‎or https://img.pvme.io/ ‎(via [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/771436827214086154 Guide media upload and request (external Discord)])

⬥ Add angled brackets <> ‎around links to prevent them showing inline

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• For example, [Greater Fury](<https://runescape.wiki/w/Greater_Fury>)​

​

Useful Markdown & GitHub Syntax

⬥ ‎`code` ‎ ‎for inline code

⬥ .img:<url> ‎for images

⬥ .tag:sectionName ‎for ToC section targets

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• $linkmsg_sectionName$ ‎for linking to that section

​

Filenames

⬥ Filenames should follow these naming patterns:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Basic guides: {bossName}-basic.txt​

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Combat Achievements: {bossName}-ca.txt​

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Commands: {commandName}.txt​

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• DPM Advice: dpm-advice-{style}.txt​

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• One-tick guides: {bossName}-one-tick.txt​

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Full Boss guides: {bossName}-{difficulty}-{style}.txt​

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ {difficulty} ‎is optional; either hm ‎or nm​

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ {style} ‎is optional; either ranged, magic, melee, necromancy, hybrid​

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Slayer: {monsterName}.txt​

​

⬥ If not listed above, hyphenate the title:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• e.g., interface-guide.txt​

​

⬥ These naming patterns should also apply if the file is inside the boss folder, e.g. /sanctum/sanctum-hm-ranged.txt​

​

Presets

⬥ Create and link to presets in our Preset Maker tool ([[PvME/Contributing/Preset Maker|Preset Maker]])

⬥ Multiple presets may be created for different situations

⬥ Links to presets should be in the following pattern:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• {Combat style} - {Basic/Advanced/Tier}​

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ e.g., [[PvME/Contributing/Style Guide|Necromancy - Basic]] / [[PvME/Contributing/Style Guide|Necromancy - T95/100]]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Only the last link should be shown - the rest should be hidden by wrapping the link in <>:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ e.g., [https://presets.pvme.io/?id=presetID https://presets.pvme.io?id=presetID]

⬥ Avoid dyed gear or overpriced items which do not feature in [https://pvme.io/gear/ Upgrade guides]

⬥ Be consistent with:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Rune pouch colours ([[PvME/Gear upgrades/Armour And Weapons|Armour And Weapons]])

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• EoF emojis ([[PvME/Combat reference/Eof Specs|Eof Specs]])

​

Using Notes in Presets

⬥ Notes relating to specific preset gear/items should be added to the Preset Maker

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Do not add notes to the guide, for example below the Preset image

​

⬥ Add a note for any non-standard gear or niche items

⬥ Add a note on any gear where perks differ from standard ones listed in [[PvME/Invention perks/Perks|Perks]]

​

⬥ For AFK guides, notes may be added to the Mandatory AFK Requirements ‎embed for:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Required ability unlocks (including [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1148995625896120460.png?v=1 necromancy] Talent Tree)

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Mandatory gear/items differing from those listed in [[PvME/Lower-effort methods/AFK Overview|AFK Overview]]

​

Rotations

⬥ Use [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pvme/pvme-settings/master/emojis/emojis.json full emoji codes], e.g., <:emoji:ID>​

​

⬥ Use + ‎to combine same-tick actions, e.g., [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/655341074235129858.png?v=1 vulnbomb] + [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1159434663903899728.png?v=1 deathskulls]

​

⬥ Use → ‎to separate ticks and GCDs, e.g., [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541270521708566.png?v=1 rapid] → [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535534127131394088.png?v=1 snap]

​

⬥ Use () ‎for:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Target cycle (tc)

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Auto attacks (auto)

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Waiting (2t) - ticks are from previous action

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Channel durations (3 hit)

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Weapon types (DW) / (2H)

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Autocasting ([https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/856635090745950258.png?v=1 exsanguinate])

​

⬥ Include non-ability actions, e.g., [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/655341074235129858.png?v=1 vulnbomb] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/736298121704767538.png?v=1 adrenrenewal] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/641339922019516416.png?v=1 undeadslayer] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/641339921814126594.png?v=1 dragonslayer] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/641339921675845633.png?v=1 demonslayer] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/537336877900890135.png?v=1 nip]

​

⬥ Use s ‎and r ‎to represent stall & release, e.g.:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• s<ability> → r<ability> + <nextability>​

​

⬥ Use [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/537340400273195028.png?v=1 spec] and [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1257438999794946099.png?v=1 eofspec] properly, e.g.:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Weapon specs: <:sgb> <:spec> ‎[https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/626466665848242186.png?v=1 sgb] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/537340400273195028.png?v=1 spec]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• EOF specs: <:sgb> <:eofspec> ‎[https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/626466665848242186.png?v=1 sgb] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1257438999794946099.png?v=1 eofspec]

​

⬥ Show ammo swaps before and after abilities, e.g.:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Single ammo switch: [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/867678153966878740.png?v=1 gricocaroming] → [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/971025696958853180.png?v=1 fularrow] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/626466665848242186.png?v=1 sgb] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1257438999794946099.png?v=1 eofspec] → etc.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ Includes off-style abilities: [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/550834403136503822.png?v=1 hydrixbakri] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/867678153966878740.png?v=1 gricocaroming] → etc.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Multiple ammo switch (like "wensporing"): [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/867678153966878740.png?v=1 gricocaroming] → [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/971025697046925362.png?v=1 wenarrow] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/643848618553507843.png?v=1 dbow] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1257438999794946099.png?v=1 eofspec] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/900758234527301642.png?v=1 deathsporearrows] → etc.

​

⬥ 0-tick abilities should follow this pattern:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1266417538045317121.png?v=1 roarofawakening] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/537340400273195028.png?v=1 spec] (0tick)

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Add a note pointing to the !0tick ‎command

​

Table of Contents (ToC)

⬥ Each guide ends with a pinned ToC section

⬥ ToC is always within a Discord embed

⬥ Must be pinned – add .pin:delete ‎under it

⬥ The easiest way to create a ToC is to add a .tag: ‎after all relevant headings, then auto-generate your ToC using the Table of Contents ‎feature on the [https://pvme.io/guide-editor/ Guide Editor] (see image below)

[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

This guide showcases many of the ways you can be more efficient when writing guides, whether that be through copy-able templates, code snippets or other tips.

​

It assumes you are using the [https://pvme.github.io/guide-editor/ PvME Guide Editor] to write & live preview your guides.

​

Finding and using Templates

In the Guide Editor toolbar you will see a "Template" dropdown, containing starting points for our main guide types:

⬥ Boss Guide

⬥ AFK Guide

⬥ Slayer Guide

⬥ Command Embed

​

Simply click "copy" and paste these into the editor to get started on your guide, as in the screenshot below:

[https://img.pvme.io/images/ArqoW60TuE.png Guide illustration] ​

Finding emojis

There are two ways to find an emoji:

  1. In the Guide Editor, simply start typing :emojiname ‎and it will bring up a list - select the one you want

  2. Search the full repository of emojis at [https://pvme.io/pvme-settings/#emojis https://pvme.io/pvme-settings/#emojis]

​

Linking items to the Wiki

Many of our guides link items and gear to the [https://runescape.wiki/ RS Wiki]. Follow these steps:

⬥ Use the pattern: [Item name](<http://runescape.wiki/w/Item_name>) <:emoji:>​

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Wrap the URL in <> ‎to prevent it showing a preview

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Most items only capitalise the first word

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Replace spaces with underscores

⬥ Test your URL in the guide editor by clicking on it

​

See the following example:

​[Channeller's ring](<http://runescape.wiki/w/Channeller's_ring>) <:channellersring:839903943404027914>​

→ [http://runescape.wiki/w/Channeller's_ring Channeller's ring] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/839903943404027914.png?v=1 channellersring]

​

Using Embeds

Sometimes we use a special Discord "embed" to format messages in a pretty way - these are written in JSON. When inside a JSON, common punctuation like bullets or new lines will not work as normal; use the following to achieve what you are looking for:

​

⬥ \n → adds a new line

⬥ \u00a0\u00a0\u00a0\u00a0 = adds a new line + 4 spaces

⬥ \n⬥ → adds a new line + a bullet

⬥ \n\u00a0\u00a0\u00a0\u00a0• → adds a new line + 4 spaces + a sub-bullet

⬥ \n\u200B → adds a blank line

​

A example embed can be seen below:

​

..
{
  "embed": {
    "title": "__[embed title]__",
    "description": "[embed description]\n\u200B",
    "color": 39423,
    "fields": [
      {
        "name": "__[field 1 name]__",
        "value": "[field 1 contents]"
      },
      {
        "name": "__[field 2 name]__",
        "value": "⬥ Field 2 contents\n⬥ Field 2 contents"
      }
    ]
  }
}
..embed:json

​

When rendered, the above code looks like the following;

[embed title]
[embed description] ​
[field 1 name]
[field 1 contents]
[field 2 name]
⬥ Field 2 contents ⬥ Field 2 contents

​

[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

Introduction

GitHub is a service that lets users maintain a repository of information that is organized, version controlled, and allows for easy contributions from many users. PvME uses GitHub to maintain its guides and information.

​

This guide covers how to use GitHub for contributing to PvME. If you would like to directly skip to the instructions, you can directly navigate to the Tutorial section using the pinned links, and if you would like a quick tutorial, use [[PvME/Contributing/Github Quick Guide|Github Quick Guide]].

​

Once you have completed this tutorial, you can look at [[PvME/Contributing/Github Tips And Troubleshooting|Github Tips And Troubleshooting]] for more tips, tricks, and other information.

​

How GitHub Works

⬥ GitHub is an Internet hosting service that offers the use of Git repositories, which is how PvME stores its information and guides.

⬥ A repository is a collection of all the files and folders for a project, that is tracked and version controlled.

⬥ Anyone can contribute to the PvME repository.

⬥ The basic contribution process looks like this:

fork PvME repo → make changes → commit changes → make pull request → changes get accepted

⬥ A brief explanation of the steps:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Make a copy of the repository, also known as forking the repository. You now have an up-to-date copy of the PvME files.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Make changes to the files in your repository and commit them to your own repository. You can think of this as "saving" your changes.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• To add your new changes to the PvME repository, make a pull request. This tells PvME that you have changes you want pulled from your files into PvME's files.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Wait for your pull request to be accepted. When this is done, your changes will now be a part of PvME's guides!

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• You can now re-sync, or delete and re-fork the repository once you want to make more changes.

​

Tutorial

The goal of this tutorial is to add your name to the list at the bottom of this guide.

​

Step 1: Create a GitHub Account ([https://github.com/ https://github.com])

⬥ Go to GitHub and use the Sign Up button on the top right of the page.

⬥ Your username and e-mail account will be visible, so ensure you don't include personal information.

⬥ If you have a GitHub account already, it is advised to make a new one for PvME unless you are certain that you haven't doxxed yourself in your commit histories.

For experienced users: If you use the Git CLI, make sure you check your git config [user.name|user.email] ‎configs, as these settings can still dox you, even if you use a new account.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/uI7JVfh.png Guide illustration]

Step 2: Fork the PvME Repository ([https://github.com/pvme/pvme-guides https://github.com/pvme/pvme-guides])

⬥ This creates a personal copy of the repository that you can then edit at your leisure.

⬥ Click the Fork button at the top right of the page, then confirm the creation of the fork.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/9sDym3q.png Guide illustration]

[https://img.pvme.io/images/TenWOom.png Guide illustration]

Step 3: Open Your Forked Repository In Your Browser

⬥ You can find it by selecting Your Repositories in the dropdown menu, found by clicking your profile at the top right.

⬥ You will know you are in your forked repository when the top-left of the website looks like this:

[https://img.pvme.io/images/h0zk8pQ.png Guide illustration]

For experienced users: You can just clone the repository locally and work from your local machine, whatever you prefer.

Step 4: Navigate to the github-tutorial.txt File

⬥ The structure of the PvME repository mimics the server category/channel structure, to navigate through the repository click through folders that share the name of the discord categories, until you find this guide in the GitHub repository.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• If you are struggling to find a file you can use the search bar at the top.

⬥ The file is located at editor-resources > github-tutorials > github-tutorial.txt.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/tT47C8Y.png Guide illustration]

Step 5: Enable Discord Developer Options and Copy Discord ID

⬥ This is required to be able to copy your own Discord ID.

⬥ These settings are accessible at Discord App Settings > Advanced > Developer Console > (turn on).

⬥ After enabling them, you can right-click your name or profile picture to copy your own Discord ID.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/fUd2Z3a.png Guide illustration]

[https://img.pvme.io/images/17NA9pa.png Guide illustration]

[https://img.pvme.io/images/uK0diGu.png Guide illustration]

Step 6: Your First Change and Contribution

⬥ Click the Edit icon at the top right to begin editing the file. It looks like a pencil.

⬥ Paste your Discord ID at the bottom of the file, below the other IDs, in the format <@yourusedidhere>.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Replace the text with your Discord ID.

⬥ Then commit (i.e. save) your changes.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Leave the settings at their default (i.e. "Commit directly to the master ‎branch").

[https://img.pvme.io/images/SFB0OqA.png Guide illustration]

[https://img.pvme.io/images/EKpuYym.png Guide illustration]

Step 7: Create A Pull Request

⬥ Navigate to the Code tab in your personal repository. You will notice that you are now 1 commit ahead - this means you have changes ready to contribute!

⬥ Click the Contribute button and select Pull Request from the drop-down.

⬥ You can add type something like "add my name to github-tutorial" as the commit message, and then create the pull request.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/DXYZid4.png Guide illustration]

[https://img.pvme.io/images/696GEzw.png Guide illustration]

Step 8: That's it!

⬥ You're done! If your changes are approved, then your pull request will be merged into PvME.

⬥ The [[PvME/Contributing/Github Comp Tutorial|Github Comp Tutorial]] channel will get updated, and your name will appear in the channel.

⬥ You can resync or delete your fork after the pull request is accepted. To delete a fork, go to your repo Settings, and scroll down till you find the option to delete. Then follow the confirmation process.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/VpO5Lde.png Guide illustration]

[https://img.pvme.io/images/YaxlO8O.png Guide illustration]

[https://img.pvme.io/images/a1HmkID.png Guide illustration]

[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

Introduction

All of our guides are hosted on GitHub, this is an online service which allows for anyone to make changes to our guides.

​

Before starting there are two important things to know:

⬥ Don't be scared, you wont break anything!

⬥ If you are unsure about anything feel free to ping a member of the editing staff in [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/724129126314803230 Editors chat (external Discord)]

​

Note: Make sure that your GitHub account DOES NOT dox you. It is recommended to use a separate account to work etc, as username and email are visible.

Your First Edit
Ask questions if you get stumped Bolded and Indented text will change for future edits, but the procedure is the same! For a visual guide, check [https://youtu.be/6sTpzSYtVQI this video], feel free to follow along to make your first edit.
Setting up to Edit
⬥ Get your own copy of repository on github (fork the repository)     • Go [https://github.com/pvme/pvme-guides here], make an account, then click fork at the top right. ⬥ Find the github-tutorial file (use the search bar at the top) and copy it     • You can also manually navigate the folders (editor-resources/github-tutorials) to find it.     • This may be needed just after you fork the repository. ⬥ Paste the guide into the [https://pvme.github.io/guide-editor/ Guide Editor]
Making the Changes
⬥ Add your name to the bottom of the 'completed github tutorial' list     • To add your name, type <@id> replacing id with your discord id     • To get your id you need to enter developer mode (settings, advanced, turn on developer mode)     • Click my account, and then using the three dots next to your name, copy user id ⬥ Save the edited guide to a .txt document on your computer ⬥ Head to bot test, type pvme$txtpost, and attach your document ⬥ Check everything works
Submitting them to GitHub
⬥ Edit the guide in your Repository with your change     • The edit button is on the top right ⬥ Commit these changes     • The commit button is on the top right ⬥ Head to the homepage of your repository     • Click <>code on the top left ⬥ Click contribute ⬥ Click open pull request ⬥ Make sure the title explains the changes you are making ⬥ Click create pull request ⬥ Done!

From here one of our editing staff will review the pull request, check that everything works, and then merge it into PvME!

​

Note:* The first step in "Setting up to Edit*" only need to be done the first time!

Whats Next?

Head into [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1152990486714388622 Editing jobs (external Discord)] and have a look at the jobs! We recommend you find an easy one and just give it a go! Make sure to message or ping Editing Staff (community role) in [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/724129126314803230 Editors chat (external Discord)] if you need help.

​

Have a look at the tools and references that are available in Referenced guide unavailable in this snapshot. Don't feel the need to read through all of them, just have a look what you think will be useful to you.

pages.text:
[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

Introduction

This guide will go over an assortment of common issues you may encounter while working with GitHub, as well as a few helpful things you can do to streamline your workflow.

Note: You can always ask any editor or staff for help with GitHub at any time.

​

Frequently Used Terminology

⬥ Repository

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• A collection of all the files and folders for a single project, that is tracked and version controlled.

⬥ Fork

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• A copy of an entire repository. A user can fork a repository to get a personal copy.

⬥ Commit

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Essentially a 'snapshot' of your repository. Think of it like a checkpoint in a video game. Going back to a particular commit shows the entire repository as it was at that point in time. You commit after making your changes, to prepare for a pull request.

⬥ Pull Request

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• A request to merge your changes into the main repository, to be accepted by someone with appropriate permissions.

​

Common Problems

Failed Checks

⬥ PvME GitHub is set up to automatically check for valid formatting and styling. There are a number of checks, such as:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Trailing whitespace - extra space at the end of a line

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Improper spacing around emojis - emojis must be surrounded by a space on either side

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Message length exceeded (too many characters) - messages cannot exceed 2000 characters

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Invalid embed formatting - creates an invalid embed object.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Invalid commands - any .command: ‎used must be a valid command.

⬥ Checks failing can be avoided by using the web editor ([https://pvme.github.io/guide-editor/ https://pvme.github.io/guide-editor/]) to edit your content before adding it to GitHub, as it runs the same style checks that pull requests use. For more information check out, [[PvME/Contributing/Guide Editor|Guide Editor]].

⬥ If your pull request fails due to a check, it will inform you. Click on Details on the check to see why it has failed, and what you can do to fix it.

⬥ Consider the following example:

[https://img.pvme.io/images/ZxizF57.png Guide illustration]

[https://img.pvme.io/images/qdZjUvf.png Guide illustration] ⬥ The bottom red square tells you what the error is. In this case, the message starting at line 108 and ending at line 139 has too many characters.

⬥ To fix this, click the Edit File option in the following image, to open up editing again to make appropriate changes.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/WHpF7Wq.png Guide illustration] ⬥ In this case, we break the single large message into 2 separate messages by hitting Enter, entering a single period . ‎and hitting Enter ‎again. Then commit these changes, and it will update the pull request.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/fTIpYv5.png Guide illustration] ⬥ Your Pull Request should now be error-free once the checks complete again.

​

Checks Are Stuck

⬥ Rarely, the style and syntax checks may get stuck, neither succeeding nor failing. In such an event, usually merging a different minor pull request tends to resolve the issue.

⬥ Checks can take some time to complete at times, so wait for at least 20-30 minutes before it is considered an issue.

⬥ In case this occurs, you can contact an editor or staff for assistance.

​

Your Branch Is 'X' Commits Behind Master

⬥ When you make a new fork, your fork will look like this:

[https://img.pvme.io/images/j3kEy55.png Guide illustration] ⬥ However, after some time it may look something like this:

[https://img.pvme.io/images/ztJQ0wj.png Guide illustration] ⬥ This is because changes might have happened to the main repository ('X' commits behind) and it is no longer in-sync with your copy. This may cause issues when making a pull request.

⬥ To resolved this, the simplest solution is to delete your fork, and make a new fork of the PvME repository.

⬥ This will give you a fresh, up-to-date copy, and get rid of any lingering issues.

​

For more experienced users: PvME squashes and merges all pull requests. This causes a difference in commit hashes, which is why your branch will be both ahead AND behind in commits after a pull request is accepted. You can clean this up by discarding commits from accepted PRs and syncing your branch to pvme:master. Or by resetting your branch to pvme:master. Or just delete and start over.|

​

Pull Requests

Multiple Changes & Updating an Existing Pull Request

⬥ It is possible to include changes to multiple files within the same Pull Request, and to amend files you have already modified as part of that Pull Request.

⬥ This can be helpful to reduce the number of PRs being opened, and remove the need of closing a PR and reopening it if a mistake has been made.

​

Note: It is assumed you have already forked the repository.

​

⬥ Consider the scenario: a pull request has been made, with changes to one file, visible in the Files Changed tab.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/kxvu0O2.png Guide illustration] ​

Modify an Existing File in the Pull Request

To make an a change to a file that already contains a change, in the same pull request, do the following.

⬥ Navigate to your Pull Request, and go to the Files Changed tab.

⬥ Go to the top right corner of the file you wish to update, click the three dots, then Edit File.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/h2i3Rkb.jpg Guide illustration] ⬥ Make whatever additional changes you like, and then Commit directly to the xxx branch.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/GbkYLNi.png Guide illustration] ⬥ Navigate back to your Pull Request, and the additional change should be included!

[https://img.pvme.io/images/OxtPQXE.png Guide illustration] ​

Add a New File to the Pull Request

To edit a different file, and include it in the same pull request, do as follows,

⬥ Navigate to your Pull Request and click on the name of your branch, here:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• You are now looking at the main directory of your own branch, where all files will reside.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/ylNa85w.png Guide illustration] ⬥ Locate the additional file you would like to change, open it, and then click the edit icon.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/kSt0Xpa.png Guide illustration] ⬥ Make whatever changes you like, and then Commit directly to the xxx branch.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/sa6tPYh.png Guide illustration] ⬥ Navigate back to your Pull Request, and the additional file should be included!

[https://img.pvme.io/images/UKnKrfs.png Guide illustration] ​

Helpful Tips

File Split View

⬥ When opening a Pull Request, it is good practice to look at your changes and see if any mistakes have been made.

⬥ By default, you will see differences between your changes and the original file in Unified View.

⬥ Sometimes, especially for larger changes, it can be helpful to use Split View instead.

⬥ Navigate to your Pull Request, and go to the Files Changed tab.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• By default, you will see unified changes, as shown below:

[https://img.pvme.io/images/KqtUExJ.png Guide illustration] ⬥ Click the settings icon, select Split, and then Apply and reload.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/mqNCNlT.png Guide illustration] ⬥ Congratulations! From now on, your changes will be shown in Split View.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• You can reverse the process to go back to a unified view at any time, if you prefer.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/IAz8bya.png Guide illustration] ​

Bulk Replacing

⬥ To bulk replace, either navigate to the Edit menu then select Replace in Files or use the Ctrl+Shift+H keybind to do the same.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/avBqR0i.png Guide illustration] ⬥ Doing this will open the Search/Replace side menu.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/bLoBXsg.png Guide illustration] ⬥ The search box is where you enter what you want to replace and the replace box is where you enter what you want to replace it with.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/1aRteP5.png Guide illustration] ⬥ However, most of these results aren't what we're looking for so can be dismissed by hovering over the number to the right and clicking the X to dismiss the whole file or the individual Xs below to dismiss individual matches.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/acVwcaR.png Guide illustration] ⬥ When you find something you want to replace. you can either right click and click Replace to do it one at a time or you can click the icon to the left of the X to replace all matches in a file.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/wolcMdJ.png Guide illustration] ​

[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

Introduction

Welcome to our Feats System channel, the purpose of these challenges is to give you fun objectives to aim for at various encounters, aiming to provide a challenge disregarding any meta whatsoever of farming kills. Happy hunting!

​

All submissions require supporting evidence to be reviewed by staff.

​

Submitting for a Role

A submission should be provided as follows, with your in-game name visible:

⬥ Feat name

⬥ Supporting video evidence

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Only videos are accepted unless otherwise stated

Feats System Rules
⬥ All rules used by the [https://discord.gg/AR5qErBGDs PvM Records (external Discord)] community apply     • Full list is available [https://www.pvm-records.com/rules here].     • Any new bugs/exploits added to the [https://www.pvm-records.com/rules list] that are used prior to being disallowed may result in submission denial. ⬥ Power creep may place submissions on hold. ⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Deathtouched_dart Deathtouched darts] are not allowed for any feat..

Seasonal Feats

These temporary feats will regularly rotate with new choices and are for the real feat lovers.

Current season: September 2nd - December 31st

​

Rooted in Fear (community role) ⬥ Defeat Beastmaster Durzag solo without kiting him     • Does not need to include the horde A Catastrophe (community role) ⬥ Defeat Amascut at 4,000% enrage while entering phase 7 with 9m+ hp Coven's Curse (community role) ⬥ Defeat Zamorak at 4,000% enrage without using an ultimate ability

PvME Special Roles

⬥ "Roles" = Feats only ⬥ Seasonal feats are not required for these roles
Available Roles
Party Queue (community role)     • Obtain all feats up to and including Adept tier Feat Enjoyer (community role)     • Obtain all feats up to and including Master tier Featured (community role)     • Obtain all feats up to and including Grandmaster tier deFeated (community role)     • Obtain all feat roles
[https://img.pvme.io/images/EPzzJe2xy6.gif Guide illustration]

Please post your submissions in [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/827692629197324348 Role submissions (external Discord)] so that they can be reviewed by staff and/or role reviewers. Submissions will be evaluated according to our rules, as follows:

Initiate Feats

These feats are for those who mastered the basics of a boss and want to start pushing themselves further.

​

Killer Tick (community role) ⬥ **Kill 1 boss in the least ticks possible as recognised by [https://www.pvm-records.com/ PvM Records] nopenope (community role) ⬥ Complete a solo Araxxor kill while executing a top path heal skip Solo BM (community role) ⬥ Solo Beastmaster Durzag**     • Must include the hoard Nature's Wrath (community role) ⬥ Defeat Solak with the Wrath curse dealing the final blow     • For this you must die to the instakill attack caused by Solak's mind dying
Duo Mirage (community role) ⬥ Duo Yakamaru (Mirage phase) Fight Club (community role) ⬥ Complete a hardmode Tzkal-Zuk run after clearing the triple jad wave with only your fists Skippy McSkipface (community role) ⬥ Kill Seiryu in a single cycle, skip the BSD flight phase, and skip the Ambassador spinner phase in solo instances.     • In a row not required

​

Adept Feats

A stuntman rises from the ashes. The encounters in this bracket will test your game knowledge and combat improvisation.

​

Gold Daredevil (community role) Achieve [https://img.pvme.io/images/vJcULD6YNr.png Golden Daredevil]     • A list of the daredevil feats can be found [https://runescape.wiki/w/Hero_of_the_Goebies here]     • A screenshot of the achievement in the CA interface can be used in place of a video True Warden (community role) ⬥ Kill Telos at 4000% enrage Frostbite (community role) ⬥ 200ks at Arch-Glacor     • Screenshot is acceptable
nopenopenope (community role) ⬥ Complete the Lumbridge strikes back [https://runescape.wiki/w/Lumbridge_Strikes_Back achievement] at 300% enrage on the top path of Araxxor     • Must use a [https://runescape.wiki/w/Spirit_spider Spirit Spider] familiar Solo Vorago NM 6/6 (community role) ⬥ Solo Vorago NM on all 6 weeks Silver Defeater (community role) ⬥ Duo Vorago HM on all 6 weeks Lord of Chaos (community role) ⬥ Kill Zamorak at 4000% in a group

​

Master Feats

The Daredevil rises. Your consistency is unparalleled and your guts immeasurable.

​

Last Man Standing (community role) ⬥ Defeat 4000% enrage Telos after killing all minions that spawn on phases 4 and 5 Ice Cold (community role) ⬥ Kill Arch-Glacor at 4000% enrage Wrath of Chaos (community role) ⬥ Kill Zamorak at 4000% enrage in solo
Animaster (community role) ⬥ 200ks at Telos     • Screenshot is acceptable Zarosian Prodigy (community role) ⬥ Solo AoD Solo Mirage (community role) ⬥ Solo Yakamaru (Mirage phase) Master of Omens (community role) ⬥ Solo Hard Mode Vorago God of Destruction (community role) ⬥ Kill Amascut at 4000% enrage

​

Grandmaster Feats

Some would call you crazy, others a madman. We prefer to call you a Feats Fiend.

​

Golden Defeater (community role) ⬥ Solo Hard Mode Vorago on all 6 weeks True Animaster (community role) ⬥ 200ks at Telos with 4000% enrage start     • No darts allowed     • Must provide VODs + chests + quick chat KC         ⬩ Provide this for any kill between 2nd-10th AND final kill Emberstruck (community role) ⬥ Defeat Zamorak at 4000% enrage without overhead prayers or food [https://youtu.be/ekJYq_BdmgU demo]     • No infernus teleporting during green/red hp allowed Anima-bound (community role) ⬥ Defeat Telos at 4000% enrage without overhead prayers or food [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G4AjKKHb_Y8 demo] Twisted Tails (community role) ⬥ Kill Amascut at 2000% enrage as a Duo     • Must intercept every blinking strike on phase 5 after reforming Tumeken

Insane Feats

Only the most reckless fighters would attempt such encounters, consistency and extreme skill are in display for the most gruelling challenges in this bracket.

​

Eternal Frostbite (community role) ⬥ 200ks at Arch-glacor with 4000% enrage start     • No darts allowed     • Must provide VODs + chests + quick chat KC         ⬩ Provide this for any kill between 2nd-10th AND final kill Messiah of Mazcab (community role) ⬥ Achieve [https://img.pvme.io/images/vJcULD6YNr.png Golden Daredevil] in duo     • A list of the daredevil feats can be found [https://runescape.wiki/w/Hero_of_the_Goebies here]     • This includes puzzle completion Hypothermic (community role) ⬥ Defeat Arch-Glacor at 4000% enrage without overhead prayers or food [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JTL-hAvp0_A demo] A Tail of Two Cats (community role) ⬥ Kill Amascut at 4000% enrage as a Duo     • Must intercept every blinking strike on phase 5 after reforming Tumeken

​

[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

Here, we welcome any suggestions you want to make on improving the server! See below for steps and tips on making suggestions.

​

Categories

⬥ Guide suggestion - Suggestions for guide content or structure (e.g. updated rotations, deleting a redundant section).

​

⬥ Server suggestion - Suggestions for server operations or structure (e.g. improvements to the vod review process, shifting of channels).

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Use [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/820143052227346442 Modmail (external Discord)] for more sensitive topics.

​

⬥ Command suggestion - Suggestions about changing/introducing commands

​

⬥ Typo Fix - Suggestions highlighting typos to be fixed

​

⬥ Mastery/Feats - Suggestions about changing/introducing feats or masteries.

​

Making suggestions

Below outlines the process and suggested steps of making suggestions.

​

  1. Enter the title in the search bar and click "New post".

[https://img.pvme.io/images/19lrC0CzsW.png Guide illustration]

  1. Enter more details about suggestion (including pictures/vods can be very helpful) and mark your suggestion with relevant tags - [[PvME/Get involved/Making suggestions and editing guides#categories|Categories]]

[https://img.pvme.io/images/Alvvbay4ja.png Guide illustration]

  1. Include as many details as possible, including but not limited to:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎a. Why the suggestion is good.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎b. Possible limiting factors?

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎c. Alternative ways to implement your idea.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎d. Or even a mock-up of what it will look like once implemented.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/ynoKT4H2U6.png Guide illustration]

  1. If your suggestion thread involved a long discussion, you can provide a (point-form) summary once the discussion concludes to facilitate implementation.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/P0hUew9MR9.png Guide illustration]

  1. If you see this message, it means an editor is working on implementing your suggestion! You can return to the thread to check on its progress in the future if you find that it's taking too long.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎a. Remember, the fastest way to implement your ideas is always to edit PvME directly! Read [[PvME/Contributing/Intro To Editing|Introduction to editing]] for contributor setup.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/jfZMLxceyp.png Guide illustration]

  1. Use this link to leave suggestions anonymously - [https://forms.gle/2Q4fPrtsdCZkKEnf8 https://forms.gle/2Q4fPrtsdCZkKEnf8]

[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

Introduction

The goal of the PvME Mastery System is to allow players to set goals and track progress towards mastering specific boss encounters. Roles that are granted are kept permanently, no matter the meta that they were achieved under.

​

Mastery Roles Explained

The PvME mastery system is formed around four distinct ranks. Each rank is meant to be representative of a particular 'snapshot' in a player's journey.

​

⬥ Initiate

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Making the transition from a learner to the start of mastery; the primary goal would be to keep building familiarity with the encounter so as to continue climbing through the ranks.

​

⬥ Adept

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Once fully familiar with a boss at surface level, starts taking larger steps to understand its nuances and explores methods of optimization.

​

⬥ Master

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Displays an extensive understanding of the encounter; utilising efficient tactics with a high degree of proficiency in the relevant style(s).

​

⬥ Grandmaster

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• A true expert achieving peak performance; the most rapid, precise, and difficult tactics are leveraged with near-perfect execution with a focus on high consistency. Grandmasters can take advantage of any form of good luck they encounter to push for a faster time. A player at this skill level would be content to achieve these timers once per hour (applies more literally in some places than others).

​

Submitting for a Role

A submission should be provided as follows, with your in-game name visible:

​

⬥ Initiate / Adept

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Screenshots or videos are both accepted unless otherwise stated.

​

⬥ Master / Grandmaster

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Only videos are accepted unless otherwise stated.

​

Please post your submissions in [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/827692629197324348 Role submissions (external Discord)] so that they can be reviewed by staff and/or role reviewers. Submissions will be evaluated according to our rules, as follows,

​

Mastery System Rules
⬥ All roles requiring multiple kills will use average times. ⬥ Any timer denoted with ≤ ("sub"), e.g. "≤ 1:00", signifies that anything up until and including that time will be accepted. ⬥ Decimals are ignored entirely for all timers, including averages.     • E.g. 1:00.6 and 1:01.8 would be considered 1:00 and 1:01 = 1:00 average. ⬥ All rules used by the [https://discord.gg/AR5qErBGDs PvM Records (external Discord)] community apply     • Full list is available [https://www.pvm-records.com/rules here].     • Any new bugs/exploits added to the [https://www.pvm-records.com/rules list] that are used prior to being disallowed may result in submission denial ⬥ Power creep may place submissions on hold. ⬥ Practice mode is not allowed.

Special Roles

In addition to all of the listed mastery objectives, we provide special roles for those who go above and beyond in mastering multiple different encounters.

"Roles" = Mastery only.
Available Roles
The Go Getter (community role)     • Obtain 16 Initiate (or higher) roles The Rising Star (community role)     • Obtain 16 Adept (or higher) roles The Professional (community role)     • Obtain 16 Master (or higher) roles The Virtuoso (community role)     • Obtain 16 Grandmaster roles
[https://img.pvme.io/images/EPzzJe2xy6.gif Guide illustration]

​

Amascut, the Devourer

Amascut Initiate (community role)     • ≤ 9:00 at 500% enrage Amascut Adept (community role)     • ≤ 8:30 at 1000% enrage Amascut Master (community role)     • ≤ 6:45 at 1000% enrage Amascut Grandmaster (community role)     • ≤ 6:30 at 2000% enrage
[https://img.pvme.io/images/8vJUA2jMSu.webp Guide illustration]

​

Arch-Glacor

Arch-Glacor Initiate (community role)     • ≤ 4:00 at 1000%+ enrage Arch-Glacor Adept (community role)     • ≤ 4:30 at 2000%+ enrage Arch-Glacor Master (community role)     • ≤ 3:00 at 2000%+ enrage Arch-Glacor Grandmaster (community role)     • ≤ 5:30 at 4000% enrage
[https://runescape.wiki/images/Arch-Glacor.png?ac3e5 Guide illustration]

​

ED1: Temple of Aminishi (Solo)

Temple of Aminishi Initiate (community role)     • ≤ 1:10 Sanctum Guardian, and     • ≤ 3:00 Masuta, and     • ≤ 3:30 Seiryu Temple of Aminishi Adept (community role)     • ≤ 9:30 full run Temple of Aminishi Master (community role)     • ≤ 8:00 full run Temple of Aminishi Grandmaster (community role)     • ≤ 6:00 full run
[https://img.pvme.io/images/LbesfGr.png Guide illustration]

​

ED2: Dragonkin Laboratory (Solo)

Dragonkin Laboratory Initiate (community role)     • ≤ 1:00 Astellarn, and     • ≤ 2:00 Verak Lith, and     • ≤ 3:40 Blackstone Dragon Dragonkin Laboratory Adept (community role)     • ≤ 10:00 full run Dragonkin Laboratory Master (community role)     • ≤ 9:00 full run Dragonkin Laboratory Grandmaster (community role)     • ≤ 7:00 full run
[https://img.pvme.io/images/byVZh7g.png Guide illustration]

​

ED3: Shadow Reef (Solo)

Shadow Reef Initiate (community role)     • ≤ 1:00 Crassian Leviathan, and     • ≤ 2:00 Taraket. and     • ≤ 3:30 Ambassador Shadow Reef Adept (community role)     • ≤ 11:00 full run Shadow Reef Master (community role)     • ≤ 9:30 full run Shadow Reef Grandmaster (community role)     • ≤ 8:00 full run
[https://img.pvme.io/images/qRBpfeH.png Guide illustration]
Note: -40 seconds for Ambassador skip

​

Kerapac, the Bound (Solo HM)

Kerapac Initiate (community role)     • ≤ 3:30 Kerapac Adept (community role)     • ≤ 3:00 Kerapac Master (community role)     • B2B ≤ 2:30 Kerapac Grandmaster (community role)     • B2B ≤ 1:40
[https://img.pvme.io/images/8LRCGjz.png Guide illustration]
Note: B2B = back-to-back consecutive kills | HM = hard mode

​

Nex (Solo)

Nex Initiate (community role)     • ≤ 1:50 Nex Adept (community role)     • ≤ 1:30 Nex Master (community role)     • B2B ≤ 1:15 Nex Grandmaster (community role)     • B2B ≤ 1:05     • Dummy not allowed
[https://runescape.wiki/images/Nex.png?67c8a Guide illustration]
Note: B2B = back-to-back consecutive kills

​

Nex, Angel of Death

Nex, Angel of Death or FC trial kills are not allowed.
AoD Initiate (community role)     • ≤ 2:00 7-man, or     • ≤ 3:30 4-man or     • 7-man tag in Nex, Angel of Death Discord AoD Adept (community role)     • ≤ 1:40 7-man, or     • ≤ 2:30 4-man, or     • Member of Nex AoD FC AoD Master (community role)     • B2B ≤ 1:20 7-man, or     • B2B ≤ 1:50 4-man AoD Grandmaster (community role)     • extreme tag in Nex Aod FC, or     • ≤ 1:20 4-man
[https://img.pvme.io/images/rMbx4mo2H2.png Guide illustration]
Note: B2B = back-to-back consecutive kills

​

Raksha

Raksha Initiate (community role)     • ≤ 2:10 Raksha Adept (community role)     • ≤ 1:40 Raksha Master (community role)     • B2B ≤ 1:20 Raksha Grandmaster (community role)     • B2B ≤ 1:05
[https://img.pvme.io/images/8TO6d0O.png Guide illustration]
Note: solo or duo | B2B = back-to-back consecutive kills

​

Sanctum of Rebirth (HM)

Sanctum Initiate (community role)     • ≤ 1:40 Vermyx, and     • ≤ 2:30 Kezalam, and     • ≤ 4:00 Nakatra Sanctum Adept (community role)     • ≤ 1:30 Vermyx, and     • ≤ 2:00 Kezalam, and     • ≤ 3:00 Nakatra Sanctum Master (community role)     • ≤ 1:21 Vermyx, and     • ≤ 1:45 Kezalam, and     • ≤ 2:24 Nakatra Sanctum Grandmaster (community role)     • ≤ 1:04 Vermyx, and     • ≤ 1:20 Kezalam, and     • ≤ 1:40 Nakatra
[https://img.pvme.io/images/BAGKL7Nyq8.png Guide illustration]
Notes:     • Note 1: HM = hard mode     • Note 2: Does not need to be the same run     • Note 3: Timers are farming timers and therefore submissions including excessive prebuilds will be rejected

​

Solak

Solak Initiate (community role)     • ≤ 4:45 group, or     • ≤ 6:30 solo Solak Adept (community role)     • ≤ 3:30 group, or     • ≤ 4:30 solo Solak Master (community role)     • B2B ≤ 3:30 solo, or     • B2B ≤ 2:30 duo, or     • B2B ≤ 2:20 4s Solak Grandmaster (community role)     • ≤ 2:45 solo, or     • ≤ 2:10 duo, or     • ≤ 1:55 4s
[https://img.pvme.io/images/zrchAcA.png Guide illustration]
Note: B2B = back-to-back consecutive kills

​

Telos, the Warden

Telos Initiate (community role)     • ≤ 4:00 at 1000%+ Telos Adept (community role)     • ≤ 3:20 at 1000% Telos Master (community role)     • B2B Style camp ≤ 2:50 at 2449%+ Telos Grandmaster (community role)     • Style camp ≤ 2:20 at 2449%+
[https://runescape.wiki/images/thumb/Telos%2C_the_Warden.png/200px-Telos%2C_the_Warden.png?99e18 Guide illustration]
Note: B2B = back-to-back consecutive kills

​

TzKal-Zuk (HM)

Zuk Initiate (community role)     • ≤ 20:00 Zuk Adept (community role)     • ≤ 15:00 Zuk Master (community role)     • ≤ 13:00 Zuk Grandmaster (community role)     • ≤ 9:30
[https://img.pvme.io/images/OmNkPgY.png Guide illustration]
Notes:     • Note 1: HM = hard mode     • Note 2: -10 seconds from timer per Death Mark bug on pillars

​

Vorago

[https://img.pvme.io/images/2FyayVpTUA.png View timers] Vorago Initiate (community role)   Vorago Adept (community role)   Vorago Master (community role)   Vorago Grandmaster (community role)
[https://img.pvme.io/images/m8tni0t.png Guide illustration]

​

Zamorak: Lord of Chaos

Zamorak Initiate (community role)     • ≤ 4:30 at 200%+ enrage group, or     • ≤ 5:00 at 200%+ enrage solo Zamorak Adept (community role)     • ≤ 4:30 at 500%+ enrage group, or     • ≤ 5:00 at 500%+ enrage solo or     • ≤ 7:00 at 1000%+ enrage solo Zamorak Master (community role)     • ≤ 4:50 at 2000%+ enrage group, or     • ≤ 5:30 at 2000%+ enrage solo Zamorak Grandmaster (community role)     • ≤ 3:40 at 2000%+ enrage group or     • ≤ 4:40 at 2000%+ enrage solo
[https://img.pvme.io/images/MxjjyFAZqK.png Guide illustration]

​

Zemouregal & Vorkath (HM)

Vorkath Initiate (community role)     • ≤ 3:45 Vorkath Adept (community role)     • ≤ 2:45 Vorkath Master (community role)     • B2B ≤ 1:30 Vorkath Grandmaster (community role)     • B2B ≤ 1:00
[https://img.pvme.io/images/5EVPyccjtb.png Guide illustration]
Note: B2B = back-to-back consecutive kills | HM = hard mode

​

[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

Training buyable skills and upgrading your gear can be expensive, but there are money making methods that are effective even as a lower-level player. These are just a few methods you can try out - there are a lot more methods in the game for you to explore.

​

Note: It is assumed that you have no main account / high-level alt. If you can or want to transfer GP from another account (or purchase bonds [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513213538463121408.png?v=1 Bond]), then skip this section.

Passive Methods

These methods don't take much time and can give enough money to generate some consistent daily revenue, but are limited in how frequently they can be done. Some of these methods or locations may require quests - you do not have to go out of your way to level your skills, these are simply some of the possible options you have.

​

Combined, these methods are enough to generate a few million GP/day [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/698816156961603654.png?v=1 coins] for little time investment.

Shop Runs

⬥ Involves buying out shop stock to sell on the GE to other players.

⬥ Check the [https://runescape.wiki/w/Money_making_guide/Mega_shop_run Wiki] for all shop locations.

⬥ Starting money [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/698816156961603654.png?v=1 coins] is required.

Player-owned ports (requires one lvl 90 of [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1039864807920250900.png?v=1 thieving] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1003947795541143632.png?v=1 dungeoneering] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1005450651347730533.png?v=1 prayer] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689554435583508558.png?v=1 herblore] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1039864816073969734.png?v=1 runecrafting] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1014248190649839667.png?v=1 hunter] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1042453694735712286.png?v=1 divination] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896049548066857.png?v=1 slayer] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1011705729192820747.png?v=1 cooking] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1039864812458491924.png?v=1 construction] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1039864819760758844.png?v=1 agility] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/892342109938540564.png?v=1 fishing])

⬥ Very long-term investment, not immediate profit.

⬥ Profit comes once you have reached near the end of player-owned ports and can focus on sending your ships for trade goods like bones [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1039863294741196820.png?v=1 portsancientbones] to make tradeable scrimshaws to sell.

⬥ See the [https://runescape.wiki/w/Player-owned_port/Strategies Player Owned Ports Guide] or ask in Discord if you need help with progressing ports.

Using Invention Machines (requires 72 [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689509250946695292.png?v=1 invention])

⬥ Auto Alchemiser machines can be used to automatically high-alch items over time.

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Money_making_guide/Alchemiser_machine Alchemiser mk. II] (108 [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689509250946695292.png?v=1 invention]) is more profitable since it doesn't require fire runes, and processes more items.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Use the Wiki [https://runescape.wiki/w/RuneScape:Grand_Exchange_Market_Watch/Alchemiser calculator] to help identify items that can be bought on the GE and alched profitably.

⬥ This is passive income over time.

Skilling Methods

Non-PvM ways to make money. Note that some of these methods (e.g. crafting [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/536252658970001409.png?v=1 Bloodrune]) may require high skilling levels, so you can just choose methods that you have the levels for instead.

Runecrafting [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1039864816073969734.png?v=1 runecrafting]

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Pay-to-play_Runecrafting_training Runecrafting] high-demand runes can be quite profitable.

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Money_making_guide/Crafting_blood_runes_through_the_Abyss Blood] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/536252658970001409.png?v=1 Bloodrune] (77 [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1039864816073969734.png?v=1 runecrafting] and [https://runescape.wiki/w/Legacy_of_Seergaze/Quick_guide legacy of Seergaze] quest) and [https://runescape.wiki/w/Money_making_guide/Crafting_necrotic_runes#Spirit_runes necromancy] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1138808705362710680.png?v=1 spiritrune] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1138808701029982319.png?v=1 bonerune] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1138808695703207967.png?v=1 fleshrune] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1138808692087730206.png?v=1 miasmarune] runes (20+ [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1039864816073969734.png?v=1 runecrafting] and [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1148995625896120460.png?v=1 necromancy] and [https://runescape.wiki/w/Rune_Mythos/Quick_guide Rune Mythos] quest) are typically the most profitable runes to craft.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Recommended to have as many boosts as possible while doing this.

Croesus [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1037461776356348035.png?v=1 croesus] (recommended 80+ in [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1014248186782699541.png?v=1 woodcutting] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1014248188770787390.png?v=1 mining] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1014248190649839667.png?v=1 hunter] or [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/892342109938540564.png?v=1 fishing])

⬥ The skilling boss [https://runescape.wiki/w/Croesus Croesus] can be very good GP/hr.

⬥ Has both good common drops as well as expensive rare drops [https://runescape.wiki/w/Money_making_guide/Defeating_Croesus (link)].

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• You can use W68 public lobbies or teamforming servers/clans/etc.

Big Game Hunter (75+ [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1014248190649839667.png?v=1 hunter] 55+ [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896049548066857.png?v=1 slayer])

⬥ For example, [https://runescape.wiki/w/Big_Game_Hunter hunting] tier 1 dinosaurs for dragon mattock, or tier 2 dinosaurs to sell their meats to players doing tier 3 dinosaurs can be good profit.

⬥ This requires some practice to do efficiently ([https://runescape.wiki/w/Big_Game_Hunter/Strategies link for strategies]), but is a nice way to train the skill profitably.

⬥ Use of movement skills [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1049378668197195808.png?v=1 dive] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535533810004262912.png?v=1 surge] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541258832052231.png?v=1 escape] and the mobile perk [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689501908628799488.png?v=1 mob] is strongly recommended.

Miscellaneous methods

The further down the list, the higher the requirements generally become.

Collecting Zamorak Mjolnirs

⬥ Zamorak mjolnirs can be collected and sold for profit, with few requirements.

⬥ See the [https://runescape.wiki/w/Money_making_guide/Finding_Zamorak_mjolnirs Wiki guide] for more information.

Easy Clues [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1123586950989885510.png?v=1 easyclue]

[https://runescape.wiki/w/Clue_scroll_(easy) Easy clue scrolls] are part of [https://runescape.wiki/w/Treasure_Trails Treasure Trails], in which a player follows a series of clues leading towards a buried treasure. They're a great way to make money early on, averaging around 700k coins [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/698816156961603654.png?v=1 coins] per clue. Easy clue scrolls are between 3 to 5 clue steps long.

​

⬥ Gathering

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• You can gather them from either low-level monsters or pickpocketing [https://runescape.wiki/w/H.A.M._Hideout H.A.M. members].

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ 15 Thieving [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1039864807920250900.png?v=1 thieving] is required.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ Levelling up Thieving [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1039864807920250900.png?v=1 thieving] and Agility [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1039864819760758844.png?v=1 agility] to 50 significantly decreases your chance at failing a pickpocketing action.

⬥ Solving

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Easy clue steps (unlike the higher tiers) can always be completed.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Most of the profit from Easy Reward Caskets comes from unique items. that disassemble into [https://runescape.wiki/w/Category:Items_that_disassemble_into_Fortunate_components Fortunate] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/583435543845797891.png?v=1 fortunatecomp] components.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ Sell the items on the GE directly, usually for 1-1.5m [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/698816156961603654.png?v=1 coins] per item.

​

⬥ Clue recommendations

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Emote clues are a type of clue scroll where players perform an emote with specific items equipped. These items can be kept in [https://runescape.wiki/w/Hidey-holes hidey-holes] (27 [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1039864812458491924.png?v=1 construction]), which are storage boxes found at each clue location where they're needed.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Completing clue scrolls means travelling across Gielinor, which is why access to certain teleports can speed up this process a lot.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ The following [https://presets.pvme.io/?id=DcerXrWgcHb2RLhlzlb1 preset] from the [https://discord.com/invite/cluechasers Clue Chasers discord (external Discord)] is advised if you do decide on solving easy clues frequently.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• [https://runeapps.org/ Alt1] is a Jagex-allowed third-party application that consists of several quality of life overlays on your screen.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ One of these plug-ins is called the Clue Solver, it checks the clue you have open on your screen and tells you how to solve it.

Binding Contracts [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1073883118521557052.png?v=1 bindingcontract]

⬥ Making [https://runescape.wiki/w/Binding_contract binding contracts] to then turn into Ancient familiar pouches for profit.

⬥ Varied selection of Slayer [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896049548066857.png?v=1 slayer] monsters makes it a versatile method.

⬥ Having a way to quickly note or bank the pouches is highly recommended.

⬥ Requires the [https://runescape.wiki/w/Dagon_Bye Dagon Bye] mystery.

[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

PvM Encyclopedia is a collection of resources for RuneScape combat. This guide introduces you to how our guide and text channels are organised and presented.

Getting Involved in PvME

It's important to note that PvME is open source and everyone who wants to contribute is welcome. Regardless of your combat skill level, the editing team would love to have you! Read [[PvME/Contributing/Intro To Editing|Introduction to editing]] for contributor setup.

Navigating PvME

Text channels - Interact with other PvME users in these channels.

Social Channels
Community interactions, discuss the latest content, ask for help, post your achievements, and more!
Social Channels
[https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1082182941762924595 General (external Discord)] [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1141048675620102154 Osrs general (external Discord)] [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1141139913610362940 Other social (external Discord)] ⬥ Including: Other Games, Fitness, Coding and many more!
RS Channels
[https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/935213935999737916 Rs general (external Discord)] [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/557699151291351060 Pvm fails (external Discord)] [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/536062588090318850 Theorycrafting (external Discord)] [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/538137911292329986 Achievements (external Discord)]
Request Channels
[https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/656898197561802760 PvM help (external Discord)] [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1021152606455873686 PvM help forums (external Discord)] [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1019648841965916220 VOD reviews (external Discord)] [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/827692629197324348 Role submissions (external Discord)] [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1020853673317908500 Suggestions (external Discord)]

​

The rest of the server consists of information channels and guides.

⬥ Use the /guides ‎command to find specific guide channels. Take note to use it in [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/534563158304620564 Bot commands (external Discord)] and NOT social channels. Other methods of searching the server include:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• The Ctrl + K Discord function.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• [https://pvme.io/guides/ Guide library] which lists all channels currently maintained in PvME.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• If you've exhausted all the other options, ask in [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/656898197561802760 PvM help (external Discord)] for help.

​

PVM Help

Link: [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/656898197561802760 PvM help (external Discord)] / [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1021152606455873686 PvM help forums (external Discord)]

​

Ask all questions related to PVM or combat in these channels frequented by Helper (community role)s. They will likely know the answers to your questions or direct you to the relevant guide.

​

Some tips on channel usage:

​

⬥ Ask quick questions [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/656898197561802760 PvM help (external Discord)]. When there's an ongoing conversation which may bury your question, try using a thread or post it in [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1021152606455873686 PvM help forums (external Discord)].

⬥ Make a forum post in [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1021152606455873686 PvM help forums (external Discord)] for complex questions requiring large amounts of information, e.g. preset help, understanding fundamentals of a style or boss.

​

To help with commonly asked questions, we introduced commands. These should be used in the [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/534563158304620564 Bot commands (external Discord)] channel to provide some quick information on a variety of topics. A list of commands can be found in [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/996854552353583185 Command info (external Discord)].

​

VOD Review

Link: [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1019648841965916220 VOD reviews (external Discord)]

​

[https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1019648841965916220 VOD reviews (external Discord)] allows you to submit recordings of your PVM encounters for others to review and give constructive, personalised, and judgement-free feedback. It is a great way to improve your PVM.

​

To make a forum post in [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1019648841965916220 VOD reviews (external Discord)]:

⬥ Name it appropriately, e.g. "<Boss> (<Style>) - RSN".

⬥ Include relevant background information and/or questions.

⬥ Include a link to your video recording.

​

Bossing Path

Link: [[PvME/Learning to boss/Bossing Path|Bossing Path]]

​

The PvME bossing path provides an avenue to progress your skills and reach higher-tier PvM goals. It helps set objectives based on learning stages to measure your progression. It's perfect if you're new to bossing and unsure of where to start or looking for objectives to facilitate advancing your current abilities.

​

The Mastery System

Link: [[PvME/Get involved/Mastery|Mastery]] / [[PvME/Get involved/Feats|Feats]]

​

The PvME Mastery System is a great way to gauge your PvM progress. It provides meaningful goals to shoot for as you learn new content or hone your skills at familiar encounters. There are multiple tiers of mastery ranks, each one granting its own unique role colour for all to see.

​

PvME Boss Guides

The focus of our community is providing the best text guides possible for every encounter and players of all skill levels. Described below is the general composition of our guides. Use each guide’s On this page contents to navigate its sections quickly.

​

Header/Banner

Each guide contains a header or "banner" image, containing a few key pieces of information for each encounter. An example is show below for Osseous, the Rex Matriarch:

[https://img.pvme.io/images/EVLnU655gq.png Guide illustration]

In order of circles shown in the above example:

​

  1. Numbers represent the boss' size (for example 5x5 tiles)

  2. [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/626466665848242186.png?v=1 sgb] indicates whether the SGB special attack can be used

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Note: it is recommended to not use [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/626466665848242186.png?v=1 sgb] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/537340400273195028.png?v=1 spec] on a boss with size 1x1 or 2x2

  1. [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/841419289714229258.png?v=1 venomblood] indicates whether the boss is poisonable or not

  2. [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/583430259064569856.png?v=1 Summoning] indicates whether a familiar will be able to do damage to the boss

  3. Slayer perks ([https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689502804720615441.png?v=1 undeadslayerperk] undead, [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689502842653900818.png?v=1 demonslayerperk] demon and [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689502927731163170.png?v=1 dragonslayerperk] dragon) indicate a boss' weakness

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Note: when added as Invention perks to your gear, these will increase damage dealt to the boss by 7% and generally do not stack

​

Suggested Presets

⬥ PvME provides one or more suggested preset(s) in every strategy guide.

⬥ Historically, presets were presented as images with a link to a full breakdown of the items used.

⬥ Since the creation of [https://pvme.github.io/preset-maker/ https://pvme.github.io/preset-maker/], PvME is in the process of converting presets to a more condensed format, complete with familiars, relics, and more.

⬥ Examples of both formats can be found below.

​

⬥ Presets usually DO NOT need to be strictly copied.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Downgrading a little bit is usually fine.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• If a boss guide that has strict gear requirements that must be adhered to, it will be clearly stated.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• If unsure, ask questions relating to presets and their contents in [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/656898197561802760 PvM help (external Discord)].

⬥ Presets in full boss guides generally assume best in slot perks listed in [[PvME/Invention perks/Perks|Perks]]

⬥ Presets in basic and AFK boss guides generally assume basic perks listed in [[PvME/Invention perks/Perks|Perks]]

⬥ Downgrading your preset from the recommended may mean that rotations will need some extra improvisation.

Preset format example (Ranged HM Vorkath)

Presets and Relics

⬥ [https://presets.pvme.io/?id=89be7288-9811-4c96-8f4c-9a992d38b458 Ranged] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/580168050121113623.png?v=1 range] [https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/preset-images/o/images%2F89be7288-9811-4c96-8f4c-9a992d38b458.png?alt=media Guide illustration]

⬥ On task, prefer blue dragon / dragon cluster tasks to undead, which is depleted by minion kills

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Highest task count is blue dragons

⬥ [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/641339922019516416.png?v=1 undeadslayer] and [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689502804720615441.png?v=1 undeadslayerperk] used

⬥ [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/921410226475925514.png?v=1 hellhoundpouch] and [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/933079947419983912.png?v=1 powderofprotection] for sustain

⬥ T100 [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/994189289623662702.png?v=1 bolg] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1266418218264694954.png?v=1 shardofgenesisessence]

⬥ Use [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/971025697042755584.png?v=1 jasdragonbanearrow] on Vorkath and [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/971025696958853180.png?v=1 fularrow] on Zemouregal

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Use [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/900758234527301642.png?v=1 deathsporearrows] as needed

⬥ The following are not needed: [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615618531937222657.png?v=1 ecb] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1257438999794946099.png?v=1 eofspec] / phyical [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/626466665848242186.png?v=1 sgb] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/712073088589627505.png?v=1 eq4] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689503091539705870.png?v=1 genocidal] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/971025697046925362.png?v=1 wenarrows]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Can use [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/626466665848242186.png?v=1 sgb] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1257438999794946099.png?v=1 eofspec]

​

Mechanics & Suggested Ability Rotations

⬥ Following basic information and preset suggestions, guides will generally mention:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Specific boss mechanics.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• DPS ability rotations.

​

The rotations listed in full boss guides are designed for optimal kills!

Some considerations to take when following these are:

​

⬥ Abilities used to deal with specific mechanics should be adhered to strictly.

⬥ Most DPS rotations are generally only suggestions and need not be followed exactly

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Feel free to adapt them as you see fit!

⬥ Due to RNG you may need to improvise these rotations based on damage dealt, adrenaline etc.

​

Many of our guides make use of abbreviations. Check them out in this document: [https://runescape.wiki/w/Glossary https://runescape.wiki/w/Glossary].

​

pages.text:
[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

Introduction

Having a proper interface setup is important as it allows you to organize your game view and have quick, convenient access to game windows that you frequently interact with such as inventory, gear, familiars, ability bars and so on. A good interface can make the game easier to play and more enjoyable.

​

What is the User Interface

Creating a good interface is all about displaying the interface elements in a way where everything you need to access is open and important elements are appropriately close to one another, to minimize the distance your eyes and mouse need to travel around your screen.

​

Default Interface

The game comes with a pre-made layout, this aims to provide a usable base for every kind of player.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/HZkDZaJlB1.png Guide illustration]

Useful Interface Elements

We can observe that some UI elements are more important than others for PvM, including:

⬥ Additional action bars - gives access to a wider range of keybinds by increasing the number of action bar slots visible on-screen at any given time

⬥ Inventory - goes without saying

⬥ Worn equipment - useful to ensure correct gear is being worn, unequip armour for certain situations, activate your pocket slot items, etc

⬥ Familiar - makes it easier to track special move points, call your familiar if it's misbehaving, and make it attack faster

⬥ Spellbook - allows you to quickly switch auto-cast spell

⬥ Minimap - a larger minimap (where permissible) can make it easier to get a high-level overview of areas and navigate quickly

⬥ Chatbox - most mechanics and interactions will have some form of chat message, and keeping an eye on them can be useful. Also pairs well with the Alt1 plugin

⬥ Buff/debuff bars - keep track of all buffs/debuffs on the player

⬥ Specific style windows - it can be helpful sometimes to have additional menus open like the defensives tab, magic spellbook or style-specific ability tabs, to click on certain abilities or spells that you might not want to (or cannot) keybind

Other non-essential but nice-to-have menus include:

⬥ Skills menu

⬥ Friends list

⬥ Friends/Clan/Group chat lists

⬥ Prayers tab

⬥ Drops tab to track drops

⬥ Runemetrics tab to track statistics/damage

Creating A Good Interface

Keeping in mind the important elements of a good interface, we can use the earlier one as a reference and modify it into a layout more suitable for PvM and general gameplay. We'll do this in two broad steps - bringing into view and arranging important menus, and then using the edit layout mode to customise the interface further. Any minor tweaks or changes can be made afterwards with ease. Almost every interface element can be found by hovering the ribbon categories.

Note: This is only an example to demonstrate how to create an interface, but it is ultimately up to personal preference.

​

Step 1: Interface Layout

The first step is to set up the main menus and layout of the interface.

⬥ Unlock the interface by clicking the lock icon on the Options ribbon, or using the default keybind L

⬥ The bottom centre to the lower right is chosen as the focus for the main PvM menus

⬥ Extra action bars are added to give us more keybinds to use

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• This option can be accessed through Escape > Edit Layout Mode > Action Bars

⬥ The minimap is adjusted, and the Options ribbon is made smaller

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• The ribbon can be edited by clicking the small pencil-in-box edit icon in it

⬥ Useful PvM tabs are added around the area of focus - such as the inventory, the familiar interface, worn items, defensives, and spells

⬥ Additional menus such as the skills menu or friends list are placed in relatively accessible locations

⬥ Tabs are made large enough to eliminate extra scrollbars wherever possible

⬥ Some of the non-essential but useful menus are added and fill in any glaring gaps

Without much effort, we now have an interface that looks something like this:

[https://img.pvme.io/images/FrZsV7CK9v.png Guide illustration] The basic structure of the interface has taken shape, but there are still customisations that can be made.

Note: A portion of the game window is now covered by interface menus - this will be adjusted in the next step.

⬥ The private chat is split and placed to one side to prevent it from cluttering up the chatbox

⬥ The extra action button is kept in an easy-to-click location

⬥ The boss instance/kill timers, and slayer counter are visible and don't cover other menus
