[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

​

General Information

The goal of this guide is to guide players looking for where to start in their PvMing journey. Please note, this path isn't set in stone, because everyone learns in different ways. However, this is a decent route to follow. One thing to keep in mind is that if content starts to feel dry, or you just genuinely don't enjoy it: move on to something else. Having an enjoyable experience while learning to boss is much more important than trying to stick to a fixed list of objectives.

​

Initial combat experience can be gained by doing general Slayer at your own pace. This can be used to get the hang of combat abilities and what they do. You can also take this chance to get used to some keybinds. Alternatively, you may practice on a dummy, though you won't gain any XP or GP, and the dummy doesn't fight back!

​

Bosses with Limited Learning Opportunities

Some encounters in the game do not generally provide a great avenue to learn and improve your skills as a PvMer. These can be done for fun as you wish, however, we do not recommend them for self-improvement.

​

Bosses with limited learning opportunities
A-J
⬥ Barrows Brothers ⬥ Chaos Elemental ⬥ Corporeal Beast ⬥ Commander Zilyana ⬥ Dagannoth Kings ⬥ General Graardor ⬥ Giant Mole
K-Z
⬥ Kalphite Queen ⬥ King Black Dragon ⬥ Kree'arra ⬥ K'ril Tsutsaroth ⬥ Legiones ⬥ Magister ⬥ Rex Matriarchs

​

Bosses to Learn: Introductory

Bosses in this category serve as a great place to start in your journey to learn more about the combat system and engage in harder PvM content. While not as rewarding in terms of loot, they will provide you with many opportunities to improve your skillset.

​

Some honorable mentions that serve to teach one or two specific mechanics to players brand new to PvM:

⬥ Ivar - Teaches prayer flicking

⬥ Silverquill - Teaches reflect mechanics and dealing with minions

⬥ Flesh-hatcher Mhekarnahz - Teaches area denial and dealing with minions

​

Arch-Glacor

Arguably the best boss for overall learning, Arch-Glacor provides a customisable bossing experience. In normal mode, the player may turn mechanics on and off to learn them at their own pace. Once comfortable with a few mechanics, the player can turn many mechanics on at once to test their knowledge. In hard mode, all mechanics are enabled, with a few changes, and survivability becomes more of a challenge. In general, it is recommended to start on normal mode, progress through the mechanics, and work up to unlocking & successfully completing a hard mode kill.

​

Note: for a basic overview of Arch-Glacor, please read [[PvME/Arch-Glacor/Overview|Arch Glacor Basic]].

​

Arch-Glacor
Learning Opportunities
⬥ Build familiarity with defensive abilities, like Anticipate [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541306475151390.png?v=1 anti] and Devotion [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513190158728953857.png?v=1 devo] ⬥ Practice precise movement across a large arena. ⬥ Learn basic prayer flicking (see [[PvME/Learning to boss/Prayer Flicking|Prayer Flicking]] for an explanation), and eventually Soul Split [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit] flicking.
Introductory Milestones
⬥ Complete a normal mode kill with no mechanics enabled. ⬥ Complete five normal mode kills, each one with a different single mechanic enabled. ⬥ Complete a normal mode kill with all mechanics enabled. ⬥ Complete a hard mode kill.
Advanced Milestones
⬥ Complete a hard mode kill using no food, at any enrage, by using Soul Split [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit] flicking.     • Try to keep Soul Split [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit] active as much as possible, while flicking to Deflect magic [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/544195487926845462.png?v=1 DeflectMage], Deflect melee [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/544195488447201300.png?v=1 DeflectMelee] or Deflect missiles [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/544195488317046812.png?v=1 DeflectRange] for Arch-Glacor's auto attacks. ⬥ Complete a 25 kill streak or a 250% enrage kill, in hard mode.
[https://img.pvme.io/images/KxlQTyI.png Guide illustration]

​

GWD2: the Heart of Gielinor

While not providing as flexible of an experience as Arch-Glacor, these four bosses can provide a host of learning opportunities. They offer their own lessons and can help keep the learning process fresh, rather than just camping Arch-Glacor. In general, the difficulty of the bosses making up the GWD2 area are (approximately) equal with Gregorovic an exception (slightly harder).

​

Note: for a detailed overview of each GWD2 boss, please reference [[PvME/Gregorovic/Overview|Gregorovic Basic]] / [[PvME/Helwyr/Overview|Helwyr Basic]] / [[PvME/Twin Furies/Overview|Twin Furies Basic]] / [[PvME/Vindicta Gorvek/Vindicta Overview|Vindicta Basic]].

​

GWD2: the Heart of Gielinor
Learning Opportunities
⬥ Practice movement to avoid area of denial mechanics. ⬥ Build familiarity with defensive abilities: • Resonance [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541258844635148.png?v=1 res] (Vindicta/Helwyr)     • Freedom [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541258240786434.png?v=1 freedom] (Helwyr)     • Debilitate [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541278264393729.png?v=1 debil] and Devotion [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513190158728953857.png?v=1 devo] (Helwyr). ⬥ Become more comfortable with effectively using damage-boosting ultimates ([https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535532854004678657.png?v=1 zerk] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/994921434633744455.png?v=1 deathsswift] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/994921119381463070.png?v=1 sunshine] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1159434908486357072.png?v=1 livingdeath]) to defeat the bosses more quickly. ⬥ Learn basic prayer flicking.
Introductory Milestones
⬥ Kill each one of the GWD2 bosses. ⬥ Get three kills in a row at any GWD2 boss without banking for food.
Advanced Milestones
⬥ Complete a no-food kill at Vindicta or Helwyr, by making good use of defensive abilities.
[https://img.pvme.io/images/NTlIipw.png Guide illustration]

Osseous

Osseous provides a gentle introduction to Necromancy in an environment that fights back. There are some punishing mechanics for the uninitiated but these are quick to learn and mitigate when done correctly. Once you are comfortable with the mechanics, Osseous is a great boss to practice any damage rotation you've learned.

​

Note: for a detailed overview of Osseous, please reference [[PvME/Rex Matriarchs/Rex Matriarchs — Osseous Overview|Osseous Basic]].

​

Osseous
Learning Opportunities
⬥ Build familiarity with defensive abilities like Resonance [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541258844635148.png?v=1 res], Devotion [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513190158728953857.png?v=1 devo] and Reflect [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541258786177064.png?v=1 reflect]. ⬥ Become more comfortable using Area-of-Effect abilities at the right time ⬥ Become more comfortable with effectively using your damage-boosting ultimate and adrenaline management for rotations (Living death [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1159434908486357072.png?v=1 livingdeath]) to defeat the bosses more quickly. ⬥ Learn basic prayer flicking.
Introductory Milestones
⬥ Kill Osseous without signing or activating the Ring of Death effects. ⬥ Get three kills in a row without banking for food.
Advanced Milestones
⬥ Complete a no-food kill at Osseous, by making good use of defensive abilities. ⬥ Complete three no-food kills at Osseous in a row, by making good use of defensive abilities and damage rotations.
[https://img.pvme.io/images/UGC4GVmPyD.webp Guide illustration]

​

Bosses to Learn: Intermediate

These bosses will force you to build upon your foundations. Expect more complex mechanics, higher required damage output, and decreased survivability. Bosses are listed in approximate order of difficulty; however, you are free to pick and choose as you like. In general, all styles will be viable for each encounter, though some encounters may be easier using a specific style for the first few attempts. When in doubt, reference their associated guide for recommendations.

​

Araxxor

A very common milestone for those looking to advance into higher-tier PvM. With more complex mechanics, it will tend to punish players who are unaware of their surroundings or ability usage. It is highly discouraged to learn Araxxor in duo - it is significantly harder in a duo, and not worth doing.

​

Note: for a basic overview of Araxxor/Araxxi's mechanics, please read [[PvME/Araxxor/Overview|Araxxor Basic]].

​

Araxxor
Learning Opportunities
⬥ Become more comfortable with tracking attack patterns. ⬥ Build awareness and confidence in dealing with more complex mechanics. ⬥ Prayer flicking (especially in P4).
Introductory Milestones
⬥ Complete a 0%+ enrage kill on each of three paths. ⬥ Complete a kill at 100% enrage, on any path.
Advanced Milestones
⬥ Complete a successful kill on top path (minions) at 160%+ enrage. ⬥ At any enrage, complete phase 4 having correctly prayer-flicked each one of Araxxi's auto-attacks.
[https://img.pvme.io/images/D6q9Ubj.png Guide illustration]

​

Elite Dungeon 2: Dragonkin Laboratory

Generally considered the easiest of the three elite dungeons, ED2 provides a new kind of PvM experience: a large maze-like arena with lots of mobs, and three unique bosses. ED2 can be enjoyed alone or with friends. Due to the nature of the scaling of the dungeon, solo is considered more challenging. However, it is perfectly viable to learn in solo, as well. Players can challenge themselves to complete the dungeon faster and faster as they get more comfortable, through efficient pathing and effective usage of area-of-effect (AoE) abilities and equipment.

​

Other elite dungeons make for good options as well. After getting comfortable in ED2, feel free to explore the other two dungeons. In general, ED2 < ED1 < ED3 in terms of absolute difficulty; though, ED3's main difficulty lies in the Ambassador, its final boss. The dungeon itself is relatively straightforward compared to ED1.

​

Note: for a basic overview of the dungeon, please read [[PvME/Dragonkin Laboratory/ED2 Overview|ED2 Basic]].

​

ED2: Dragonkin Laboratory
Learning Opportunities
⬥ Learn how to effectively clear mobs using AoE damage. ⬥ Reduce food usage to eliminate frequent banking. ⬥ Improve pathing and efficiency of movement across large spaces.
Introductory Milestones
⬥ Complete a duo or trio run through the dungeon, surviving each boss encounter. ⬥ Complete a solo run, with no deaths. ⬥ Complete a solo run, having banked at most twice.
Advanced Milestones
⬥ Complete a solo run, having banked only once (or not at all). ⬥ Complete a solo run in under 40 minutes. ⬥ Earn Dragonkin Laboratory Initiate (community role).     • See [[PvME/Get involved/Mastery|Mastery]] for its requirements.
[https://img.pvme.io/images/byVZh7g.png Guide illustration]

​

TzKal-Zuk (Normal Mode)

Similar to an elite dungeon, the TzKal-Zuk encounter is comprised of more than just one boss. In this case, you will face multiple waves of enemies, before facing Zuk himself at the end.

​

After accomplishing the suggested advanced milestones, if you like, you can freely pursue hard mode for a sizeable step up in difficulty.

​

Note: for a basic overview of TzKal-Zuk, please read [[PvME/TzKal-Zuk/Tzkal Zuk Overview|Tzkal Zuk Basic]].

​

TzKal-Zuk (Normal Mode)
Learning Opportunities
⬥ Using precise positioning and defensive abilities to manage damage intake from large mobs and deadly mechanics. ⬥ Utilise different kinds of abilities in specific sequences to complete challenge waves. ⬥ Become an expert in area-of-effect ability usage to clear mobs efficiently.
Introductory Milestones
⬥ Complete a normal mode run. ⬥ Complete a normal mode run with no deaths or teleporting out.
Advanced Milestones
⬥ Complete a normal mode run in under 30 minutes. ⬥ Complete a flawless normal mode run, to unlock hard mode.
[https://img.pvme.io/images/OmNkPgY.png Guide illustration]

​

Bosses to Learn: Advanced

At this stage of your learning, there are a lot of options to further your experience and refine your skills. You can revisit previous encounters and try to push farther & faster, or, attempt to learn something harder. The following encounters are ones that we suggest you start with to make a meaningful step into becoming a high-level PvMer.

​

Raksha

This higher-tier boss encounter provides a good challenge along with the prospect of decent rewards. Raksha provides the player with the opportunity to improve multiple aspects of their PvMing skillset. It can be fought alone, or with a friend in a duo. In general, the easiest way to get your first few kills is to duo in the DPS role. After a handful of kills and becoming more familiar, it is encouraged to either start tanking in a duo or soloing. Soloing from the get-go is also perfectly viable.

​

Note: for a basic overview of Raksha, please read [[PvME/Raksha/Overview|Raksha Basic]].

​

Raksha
Learning Opportunities
⬥ Become proficient in [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit] flicking (see [[PvME/Learning to boss/Prayer Flicking|Prayer Flicking]] for an explanation). ⬥ Learning to maintain high damage output while dealing with moderately involved mechanics.
Introductory Milestones
⬥ Complete a duo kill as DPS. ⬥ Successfully [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit] flick against Raksha's auto-attacks for a whole phase. ⬥ Complete a duo kill as a tank, or complete a solo kill.
Advanced Milestones
⬥ Complete a solo kill, or duo as tank, while [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit] flicking through the entire fight. ⬥ Earn Raksha Initiate (community role)     • See [[PvME/Get involved/Mastery|Mastery]] for its requirements.
[https://img.pvme.io/images/8TO6d0O.png Guide illustration]

​

Kerapac: Hard Mode

In hard mode, Kerapac can present a serious challenge for players who aren't efficient in dealing damage and using defensive abilities. Featuring the unique Warp Time [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/870328868815396914.png?v=1 timewarp] mechanic, the encounter feels unique and has a lot of learning opportunities. Hard mode Kerapac can be enjoyed alone or with friends. The fewer the participants, the harder the encounter. It is recommended to either duo or solo when learning, as a trio does not provide enough of a challenge at this stage to be recommendable. Eventually, the goal is to solo.

​

Note: for a basic overview of hard mode Kerapac, please read [[PvME/Kerapac/Kerapac HM Overview|Kerapac HM Basic]].

​

Kerapac: Hard Mode
Learning Opportunities
⬥ Adapt to unique mechanics and leverage them as part of your damage rotations. ⬥ Sustain HP through efficient rotations and defensive ability usage, while under time pressure and dealing with high damage intake (phase 4).
Introductory Milestones
⬥ Complete a duo kill in hard mode.
Advanced Milestones
⬥ Complete a solo hard mode kill in under 6 minutes, with no beast of burden familiar. ⬥ Earn Kerapac Initiate (community role)     • See [[PvME/Get involved/Mastery|Mastery]] for its requirements.
[https://img.pvme.io/images/8LRCGjz.png Guide illustration]

​

Next Steps

If you've made it this far, you have all the tools you need to step into just about any encounter in the game. The skills you should have developed at this point include:

​

⬥ Maintaining high damage output while dealing with involved mechanics and keeping track of a boss's attack cycle

⬥ Using defensive abilities as needed to negate specific mechanics and incoming damage

⬥ Leveraging a variety of gear and abilities to deal with different scenarios and enemies

⬥ Moving efficiently throughout arenas of various sizes

⬥ Prayer flicking to both heal yourself and reduce incoming damage

​

Past this point, the content you choose to engage with is up to personal preference. When learning new content, it is important to take the same approach as this guide; that is, break your goal down into steps, and tackle them one at a time. In general, it is encouraged to try and find content that challenges you and that you genuinely enjoy doing, rather than suffering through something just to chase a drop (though, we all understand this is easier said than done).

​

Best of luck in your PvMing adventures, and don't forget to check [https://pvme.io/guides/ Guide library] for any guide you may need, and leverage [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/656898197561802760 PvM help (external Discord)] / [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1021152606455873686 PvM help forums (external Discord)] as you like.

​

[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

Introduction

Runescape PvM is relatively easy to get into but hard to master. The system is certainly not perfect, with emotionally taxing factors such as counterintuitive mechanics and a lack of phase-specific practice modes. All in all, players may be easily discouraged to continue learning PvM. This guide offers some tips to aid the learning process.

​

Approaching Runescape

Since RuneScape has a long tick system, most PvM encounters are essentially very fast rhythm games. As a result, to PvM well you must be:

⬥ Focused.

⬥ Consistent in inputs.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• A controlled attitude bolsters focus and consistency.

​

This means that you must avoid emotional or environmental factors that are distracting like:

⬥ Feeling agitated. Anger makes you a much worse PvMer.

⬥ High caffeine levels, which can cause jitteriness.

⬥ Sleep deprivation.

⬥ Being intoxicated or high.

⬥ Being dehydrated.

​

Setting Realistic Expectations

It is important to have aspirations but equally important to have realistic ones. It might take a long time before you can reach end-game levels of DPM, so it is important to set small achievable goals and take them one step at a time.

​

You might notice that the skill gap in PvM between the players can be quite large. This is not a discouraging thing! It means there is a vast PvM landscape and that you should traverse it gradually, rather than diving off the deep end as a learner.

​

Avoid Multi-task Learning

Skills like movement, prayer switches, eating food, using keybinds or executing basic ability rotations are impossible to learn all at once, as it becomes exponentially harder the more you try to do them simultaneously. Develop these skills one or two at a time to develop the muscle memory required before moving on to the next.

​

Common avenues of frustration

Here are some occurrences in PvM that tend to cause the most frustration. Acknowledge them and consider some of the suggested ways to process them to avoid anger, especially if it becomes too interfering.

​

Lethal Mechanics

Numerous bosses have mechanics that are extremely deadly and can kill you from full HP in a short amount of time unless managed properly. This can be extremely frustrating especially if one is closing in on a long kill and dying towards the end.

​

Examples include:

⬥ Solak

⬥ Telos

⬥ Kerapac

⬥ Tz-Kal Zuk

⬥ Zamorak

⬥ Nakatra

⬥ Amascut

​

Tips:

⬥ Channel your attention towards the Instakill

Often in PvM, you will find that you need to split your attention. However, when it comes to these make-or-break mechanics, switch gears and focus entirely on getting past the mechanic. Telos is a notable exception, as you are tasked to deal with many things at once during his instakill.

​

⬥ Upon death, take a moment to plan or seek advice

If you are uncertain of how to get past the mechanic consistently, explore a plan or strategy from friends or more experienced players. Engaging the encounter with a plan can make handling mechanics or DPM easier.

​

Stuns/DPS disrupting mechanics

In a game where constant ability use and specific movements are essential, bosses with stuns or other mechanics that stop you from DPSing can be massively tilting as they cause a significant disruption in combat momentum.

​

Examples include:

⬥ Kalphite King

⬥ Telos

⬥ Nex

⬥ Araxxor

​

Tips:

⬥ Do not button mash

Button mashing might make you more agitated and does not usually help the fight. Think about what to do next when you are unable to continue DPSing and deal with these mechanics calmly.

​

⬥ Learn when these mechanics occur

Usually, the most efficient way to deal with such mechanics involves properly learning the timing of the mechanic to accurately plan around it.

​

Not meeting DPS expectations/boss times

Sometimes, you might stagnate on DPS-oriented bosses, and it may seem unclear why you are not getting desired times. DPM can be unintuitive, and it is natural to be confused by a multitude of factors.

​

Bosses that may make you feel this way include:

⬥ Raksha

⬥ Kerapac

⬥ Solak

⬥ Elite Dungeons

​

Tips:

⬥ Compare and contrast with VODs

DPM is comprised of many factors that can be broken down. Compare your fights to a video of a more experienced player and break the fight down into phases.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• At each phase, note down what they are doing that you are not. Once you can identify the different factors, address each of them one at a time.

​

⬥ Try RS Analysis

RS Analysis provides insight on ability damage, lets you build rotations, and assists you in visually tracking cooldowns, damage, buff timers, and adrenaline. Check [[PvME/Combat reference/PvM Spreadsheets|PvM Spreadsheets]] for more information, or to try out other rotation builders.

​

⬥ Consider doing a Self or Peer VOD Review

Sometimes it is hard to tell your mistakes without watching back fights. Reviewing a VOD can help you or someone else catch blind spots, mistakes or correct approaches that were either missed or underappreciated. Reviewing footage across all forms of professional gaming is a well-adopted method for improvement.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Generally, submitting in [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1019648841965916220 VOD reviews (external Discord)] for peer vod review is better for remedying sub-optimal DPS than asking in [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/656898197561802760 PvM help (external Discord)]

​

Group PvM

Many players are hesitant to get into group PvM and with good reasons such as the lack of a good matchmaking system or feelings of inadequacy. However, everyone should try group pvm occasionally as it is a great way to make new friends and experience more PvM content. Here are a few tips to get you going.

​

Everyone must start somewhere

Learning bosses usually involves a great deal of dying, but do not be afraid that you will hold back your teams just because you are prone to this! Most bosses have Discords with experienced teachers to guide you through the process and their only requirement is that you are willing to listen to what they have to say.

​

⬥ Communities with active teachers include:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• RotS

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Solak

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• 7-man AoD

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Zamorak

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Vorago

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Raids

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Amascut

​

Communicate clearly

Communicate your thoughts, especially to teachers. Do not be afraid to voice out your uncertainties and weaknesses if you feel like it is necessary. If you feel like you are getting overloaded with information or are unconfident regarding a part of a fight, communicate that too clearly and respectfully.

​

Exercise patience, but do not tolerate bad behaviour

Sometimes you run into negative social experiences, such as experiencing toxic comments or having someone keep a drop they were supposed to split. Remember that these players form a very small minority of the player base and that such experiences should not prevent you from forming more friendships and enjoying social PvM in the future. Many team-forming discords also have ban lists which you can look at to see who the toxic players you should avoid are.

​

Aspects of learning

There are many different methods and mindsets to adopt when learning PvM. This section covers some of the more helpful ones to help one obtain faster progress.

​

Deliberate practice

PvM requires vast amounts of knowledge and experience to be an expert. In terms of experience, deliberate practice is the most important component of improvement. Below is a list of goals you should actively push yourself out of your comfort zone to practice if you feel that you are stagnating.

​

⬥ Keystone PvM goals (some might not be applicable to you e.g. if mobile user):

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Prayer flicking

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Revo with manual Threshold and Ultimates

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Full manual

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Two-Handed and Dual Wield swapping

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Other switches

​

These goals are dynamic. You will find yourself revisiting the basics and retheorising approaches with different bosses.

​

When trying to improve, you MUST constantly reflect on your progress to see if you are keeping on track with achieving your goals, and if not, think about what is turning out to be harder than you expected so you can start practising with a focus on those areas.

​

Skill acquisition routine

Generally, it is ideal to repeat a cycle of reading up new knowledge immediately followed by practice to see how it plays out in-game. Farming a boss without considering other players' strategies or just reading about strategies without trying them yourself is limiting your learning process.

​

Whenever feeling hard stuck, it might be worthwhile to revisit the same video or rotation as you might pick up more things that you missed previously due to having less experience.

​

Take note of mistakes after every session. Exercise self-awareness, acceptance, and actively keep track of one's weaknesses. This is the most important part of the routine.

​

Expecting a rough learning curve

Generally, one will expect their skill to always be improving, but oftentimes you will notice dips in your skill level. This is completely natural. Engaging in new skills will result in underperforming initially. This is natural and necessary to improve at PvM.

​

⬥ Some examples include:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Learning proper ECB

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Learning a new style

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Revo to full manual

​

Improvement will be slower as you progress upward. You will not always be able to improve as fast as you did initially.

​

⬥ You can mitigate this by either:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Taking on learning something that is currently way beyond your skill level (only if you are not easily discouraged).

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Make drastic changes to your PvM style to copy what you see more experienced players use.

​

Asking for help

Asking for help in PvM can be hard, but alas, sharing experiences with a more experienced player and getting feedback can make learning much smoother, here are a few things to take note of and remember.

​

Do not be scared! The first step is always the hardest. Remember, good PvMers are usually not as judgemental as you might think. Most of them have been where you are and can often offer very relevant advice on overcoming specific challenges or reaching specific benchmarks.

​

⬥ Be more open-minded/willing to try.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Helpful solutions/strategies are often plans that are not immediately obvious or require proper trial and error.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• If you receive an idea or suggestion that you feel does not apply or is too advanced, do not dismiss it immediately but keep it in mind as something to try later on.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Proactive open-mindedness allows you to fully utilise suggestions and ideas that you would have shrugged off otherwise.

​

⬥ View feedback objectively.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Take feedback given in vod reviews or trials as matter-of-fact statements and never as a personal attack on one's ability.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ Sometimes feedback you receive may seem nitpicky or blunt, this is often the result of reviewers stating their thoughts in honest details to drive across everything they think you need to know.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Most players giving feedback are NEVER trying to attack you personally or purposely acting condescending to make you feel bad. This may not be obvious especially if conveyed over text.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ At the end of the day, there are few things that make a good PvMer happier than seeing someone they helped become better.

​

Final notes

Ultimately, what is mentioned above are just guidelines. At the end of the day, RuneScape is just a game, and you can PvM however you want. Some people will simply be better at it than you by being more talented. Whenever you feel bad about your standards by comparing them with others, remember that it will NEVER define you as a person in a way that matters.

​

If you decide at the end of the day that PvM is not for you even after considering and trying out different things, there are always plenty of other things to do in RuneScape and communities to join!

​

[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

​

Introduction

This guide is intended as a guide for players looking to progress towards the tougher challenges RS3 PvM offers. It covers skill goals to set on your PvM journey, how to improve your damage and useful unlocks for your PvM experience.

​

Preparation

Before you begin, it can be helpful to get a few things out of the way:

⬥ Set up a good interface - see [[PvME/Getting started/Interface Guide|Interface Guide]].

⬥ Learn about the different combat modes (Revolution and Full Manual) - [[PvME/Learning to boss/Revo To Full Manual|Revo To Full Manual]].

⬥ Have a peek at the [[PvME/Learning to boss/Bossing Path|Bossing Path]] that you can work on as you learn PvM.

​

Initial Goals

Having an idea of some of the things you want to aim for initially can help with planning, which we cover here. None of these things are strictly necessary, but are recommended to make your bossing learning curves an easier and more enjoyable experience.

​

Skill Goals

Achieving these goals will significantly improve the variety of combat content you can successfully complete. Some suggestions on how to achieve each skilling goal can be found in [[PvME/Getting started/Noncombat Skilling Guides|Noncombat Skilling Guides]]

⬥ Level 90+ Combat Stats [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689509250472476758.png?v=1 Attack] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689509250879324165.png?v=1 Strength] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689504724159823906.png?v=1 Magic] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/580168050121113623.png?v=1 range] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689509250979987525.png?v=1 Defence] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1148995625896120460.png?v=1 necromancy]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Improves hitchance, damage, defences and survivability, and ensure you have all relevant abilities unlocked.

⬥ Level 95+ Prayer [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1005450651347730533.png?v=1 prayer]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Soul Split [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit] for healing at 92

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Damage-boosting curses [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/583429936606347280.png?v=1 turmoil] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/583429936665198592.png?v=1 anguish] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/583429936958930964.png?v=1 torment] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1137941003895046284.png?v=1 sorrow] at 95

⬥ Level 89/99 Herblore [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689554435583508558.png?v=1 Herblore]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Can boost from 89 (+7 pulse core [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1005450653390360626.png?v=1 pulsecore] boost) to make overloads [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689554436179361864.png?v=1 ovl] and use the Request Assist feature to make adrenaline renewals [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/736298121704767538.png?v=1 adrenrenewal]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Can boost from 99 (with [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1005450653390360626.png?v=1 pulsecore]) to make elder overloads [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/841419289831800882.png?v=1 elderovl], which have +4 stats over regular overloads.

⬥ Level 68+ Invention [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689509250946695292.png?v=1 Invention]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Enough to get the Starter Perks in [[PvME/Invention perks/Perks|Perks]] (with help of extreme potion [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1032540072169439242.png?v=1 extremeinventionpotion])

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Starter perks are good enough to use until you reach 120 Invention and attempt advanced perks.

⬥ Summoning [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/583430259064569856.png?v=1 Summoning] - no set level but some useful familiars are:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Hellhound [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/921410226475925514.png?v=1 hellhoundpouch] - at 45

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• War Tortoise [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513195712222068737.png?v=1 Tortoise] - at 67

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Talon Beast - at 77

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Nihils [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/854475442169053194.png?v=1 bloodnihil] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/854475441946230855.png?v=1 shadownihil] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/854475442227642388.png?v=1 smokenihil] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/854475442164334592.png?v=1 icenihil]- at 89

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Kalgerion Demon [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/921410226484301925.png?v=1 kalgpouch] - at 90

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Pack Yak [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513195712201228289.png?v=1 Yak] - at 96

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Ripper Demons [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/703581275453128714.png?v=1 ripperpouch] - at 96

​

Mid-High Level [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896050370281523.png?v=1 combat] training

The suggestions outlined below are intended for audiences wishing to go from level 50 through to 99/120 in their favourite [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896050370281523.png?v=1 combat] styles.

​

Level 50/60-80:

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Abyss/Combat_training The Abyss Monsters] (req. [https://runescape.wiki/w/Enter_the_Abyss_(miniquest)/Quick_guide Enter the Abyss miniquest]). Use AoE, [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1052551452788269127.png?v=1 protectfrommelee] if possible.

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Armoured_zombie Armoured Zombies] (req. [https://runescape.wiki/w/Defender_of_Varrock/Quick_guide Defender of Varrock quest], [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797899945730244648.png?v=1 salveamulet] works!).

Level 80+:

Worth checking [https://pvme.io/guides/?category=Slayer Slayer guides] for methods (downscale gear as necessary):

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Ravenous_ghoul Ravenous Ghouls] in the crypts below the graveyard north of Canifis.

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Vyrewatch Vyrewatch] (req. [https://runescape.wiki/w/Branches_of_Darkmeyer Branches of Darkmeyer]) [https://runescape.wiki/w/River_of_Blood/Quick_guide River of Blood quest] recommended for sunspear (pvme guide :[[PvME/Slayer/Vyres|Vyres]]).

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Bound_skeleton Bound Skeletons] north of Fort Forinthry.

⬥ [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/580168050121113623.png?v=1 range]: [https://runescape.wiki/w/Abyssal_savage Abyssal Savages] (req. 95 [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896049548066857.png?v=1 slayer]) in Wilderness or Senntisten Asylum (pvme guide: [[PvME/Slayer/Abyssal Savages|Abyssal Savages]]).

Level 95+ ([https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1096130867279171706.png?v=1 melee] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689504724159823906.png?v=1 magic] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1148995625896120460.png?v=1 necromancy]):

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Abyssal_beast Abyssal Beasts] (req. 105 [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896049548066857.png?v=1 slayer]) in Wilderness or Senntisten Asylum (pvme guide: [[PvME/Slayer/Abyssal Beasts|Abyssal Beasts]]).

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Armoured_phantom Armoured Phantoms] (req. 113 [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896049548066857.png?v=1 slayer]) (pvme guide: [[PvME/Slayer/Armoured Phantoms|Armoured Phantoms]]).

​

Bossing

⬥ If you are particularly interested in bossing, [https://runescape.wiki/w/Soul_Reaper reaper tasks] are a daily activity where Death asks you to kill a certain boss. This is a good way to experience different bosses.

⬥ You can also check out [[PvME/Learning to boss/Bossing Path|Bossing Path]] to set some bossing goals.

⬥ Basic guides for most bosses in Runescape can be found in [https://pvme.io/guides/?category=Boss%20fundamentals Boss fundamentals]. These guides have beginner preset recommendations, an overview of the boss's mechanics, and suggestions for how to deal with them.

​

Improving Damage Output

In RuneScape, the best defence is a great offence. Improving your damage output will significantly increase your chances of success at whichever boss or slayer task you're trying to accomplish. There are little things you can do to optimise once you reach that stage, but initially there are three core ways to increase your damage output:

​

⬥ Upgrading your gear setup

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Assuming a starting point of T70 weapons and T70 armour, [https://pvme.io/gear/ Upgrade guides] will help you upgrade your gear progressively for each combat style.

​

⬥ Improving your DPS rotation

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• For strong revolution bars with various degrees of ability unlocks, check out [[PvME/Combat reference/Revolution Bars|Revolution Bars]]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• For learning to switch to full manual gameplay, check out [[PvME/Learning to boss/Revo To Full Manual|Revo To Full Manual]]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• For learning how to start improving your DPM, check out [https://pvme.io/guides/?category=Damage%20%26%20rotations Damage and rotation guides]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• For help and advice, the Helpers and Super Helpers can answer your questions in [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/656898197561802760 PvM help (external Discord)]

​

⬥ Useful permanent unlocks

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Permanent unlocks have a multitude of benefits ranging from adrenaline refunds on abilities to enchantments on weapons/gear. For a full list of recommendations, check out [[PvME/Gear upgrades/Permanent Unlocks|Permanent Unlocks]]

​

pages.text:
[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

⬥ Prayer flicking is often thought of as two separate things:

​

1) ‘Prayer flicking’

⬥ Prayer flicking is changing your protection prayer to that of the boss’s current attacks (and changing the protection prayer as they change styles).This can be done on either prayer book.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• On the standard prayer book ([https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1052551452788269127.png?v=1 protectfrommelee] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1052551456835768351.png?v=1 protectfrommagic] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1052551455078367313.png?v=1 protectfrommissiles] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1137941136397324448.png?v=1 protectfromnecro]), requiring up to 46 Prayer [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1005450651347730533.png?v=1 prayer] ‎ ‎to protect from all 4 styles.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• With curses ([https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/544195488447201300.png?v=1 deflectmelee] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/544195487926845462.png?v=1 deflectmage] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/544195488317046812.png?v=1 deflectrange] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1137809111178813471.png?v=1 deflectnecromancy]), requiring up to 73 Prayer [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1005450651347730533.png?v=1 prayer] to protect from all 4 styles.

​

2) ‘Soul Split flicking’

⬥ Soul split flicking means using the Soul Split prayer [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit] most of the time, and then switching back to the protection prayer for the boss’s current attack style before the boss’s attack hits.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Soul Split flicking can only be done with curses, requiring 92 Prayer [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1005450651347730533.png?v=1 prayer] to have access to Soul Split [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit] and the 4 protection prayers [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/544195488447201300.png?v=1 deflectmelee] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/544195487926845462.png?v=1 deflectmage] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/544195488317046812.png?v=1 deflectrange] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1137809111178813471.png?v=1 deflectnecromancy]

​

⬥ This guide will cover the benefits of both prayer and Soul Split flicking, and explain how to do them!

​

Why is Prayer Flicking Useful?

Damage Reduction

⬥ Having a protection prayer up reduces your incoming damage from this style by 50%.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Increased to 60% reduction if wearing an Amulet of Souls [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513190158359724056.png?v=1 aos] or an Essence of Finality amulet [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/787526151978614824.png?v=1 eof]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• The same +10% damage reduction can be gained from powder of protection [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/933079947419983912.png?v=1 powderofprotection] if they are not wearing the amulets mentioned above. Powder and amulet effect do not stack.

⬥ Keeping the correct protection prayer up even when the boss is changing attack styles reduces the damage taken substantially.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• This reduces food usage.

⬥ When the correct prayer is active, the Devotion [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513190158728953857.png?v=1 devo] ability, as well the Devoted [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/712073087713280033.png?v=1 dev4] or Enhanced Devoted [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/712073087507628035.png?v=1 enhdev4] perk effects can be used to block 100% of the typed damage.

​

Why is Soul Split Flicking Useful?

Extra Healing

⬥ Having Soul Split [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit] active for most of the time you are attacking results in a lot of extra healing.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• This extra healing can reduce the food needed for bosses substantially, and can even remove the need to use food entirely.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• When wearing an Amulet of Souls [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513190158359724056.png?v=1 aos] or an Essence of Finality amulet [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/787526151978614824.png?v=1 eof] Soul Split has a 50% chance to heal 25-50% more for a total average of 18.75% more healing.

​

Soul Split Synergy

⬥ [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit] is required for the ECB special attack [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615618531937222657.png?v=1 ecb] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/537340400273195028.png?v=1 spec] and Necromancy Split Soul incantation [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1137809168368148490.png?v=1 splitsoul] to work

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit] flicking makes it safer and more feasible to make use of these, as you still get the benefit from [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit], but now have the heavy damage reduction of protection prayers.

​

Why is Reducing Food Usage Good?

General Benefits

⬥ Can increase room for error which makes kills more comfortable.

⬥ Increases kills per trip at bosses you do not want to teleport out of.

⬥ Reduces the supply cost for bossing.

​

Reduces Drawback of Solids and Saradomin Brews

⬥ Using solid food (e.g. sailfish [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/565726489363087360.png?v=1 sailfish]) drains adrenaline and using Saradomin brews [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/565726489400573962.png?v=1 brew] reduces stats

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Reducing the need to use them reduces the amount of adrenaline lost or stats drained throughout the course of a fight.

​

Allows You to Comfortably Swap from Beast of Burden (BoB) to DPS Familiar

⬥ You may have been using a BoB [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513195712201228289.png?v=1 yak] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1499293961364308059.png?v=1 mammothpouch] to bring more food to an encounter

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Reducing food means less need for a BoB, allowing the use of a DPS familiar [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/854475442227642388.png?v=1 smokenihil] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/921410226484301925.png?v=1 kalgpouch] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/703581275453128714.png?v=1 ripperpouch] which further reduces kill times which further reduces food usage.

​

How to Prayer / Soul Split Flick?

Advice

⬥ The most important step towards prayer or Soul Split flicking is setting up good keybinds (see [[PvME/Getting started/Interface Guide|Interface Guide]]) and using them lots to build up muscle memory.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Most people have these close together on the keyboard, near their abilities so that they can be used throughout the fight.

​

The Method

1) Look at the boss’s attack animations for the style.

2) Look at the boss’s attack rotation for attack styles (e.g. in the second phase of Vindicta [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513212949385445376.png?v=1 vindicta]).

3) When an attack animation of a style you are not currently protecting against happens, switch to that protection prayer.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/6hMspYdCZT.mp4 Source media]

4) If Soul Split [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit] flicking, switch back to [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit] after taking the reduced damage.

[https://img.pvme.io/images/euhEn55jpv.mp4 Source media]

Note: if Soul Split flicking, you want to switch from Soul Split to the protection prayer as late as possible to have Soul Split active for as long as possible, so it is good to get used to the timing of the hits to make the most out of your Soul Split time.

​

Good Places to Practice Prayer / Soul Split Flicking

⬥ Arch Glacor [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/891948878583189514.png?v=1 archglacor] normal mode with the flurry attack toggled on.

⬥ Vindicta [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513212949385445376.png?v=1 vindicta]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• 2nd phase has an attack rotation of charge → melee [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1096130867279171706.png?v=1 melee] hit → ranged [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/580168050121113623.png?v=1 range] hit → melee [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1096130867279171706.png?v=1 melee] hit

⬥ Araxxor [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513213019543699466.png?v=1 araxxi]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• This is slightly harder if using melee [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1096130867279171706.png?v=1 melee] and not standing at halberd range, as you have less time to react to its melee attacks

⬥ Raksha [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/789813907706478603.png?v=1 raksha]

⬥ Jad (Fight Caves, Kiln, or within Zuk [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/931175752651653121.png?v=1 tzkalzuk] encounter)

⬥ Any other boss you want to do!

​

Tips to Help Learning to Prayer / Soul Split Flick

⬥ Do not be discouraged if you feel you are missing a lot of prayer flicks - it is not uncommon. These skills are very rewarding, and near essential for pvm at stronger bosses, so worth learning sooner rather than later. Adding in Soul Split can come at a later stage once you're comfortable with flicking the protection prayers.

⬥ If you find yourself a little bit overwhelmed with the new keybinds, its not a bad idea to set up revo or revo++ to reduce your inputs as you start learning, and then later going back to either revo or full manual when you are more comfortable.

⬥ If you have learnt how to prayer flick, don’t be scared to give Soul Split flicking a go, even if just at bosses which attack a little bit slower.

​

Examples

Examples
Some examples of good prayer flicking.
Prayer Flicking [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1052551452788269127.png?v=1 protectfrommelee] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1052551456835768351.png?v=1 protectfrommagic] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1052551455078367313.png?v=1 protectfrommissiles] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1137941136397324448.png?v=1 protectfromnecro]
⬥ [https://youtu.be/wp-kUyZ3EN8 Prayer flicking Arch Glacor] ⬥ [https://youtu.be/bFTvc2BTUvc Prayer flicking Vindicta]
Soul Split Flicking [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/615613924506599497.png?v=1 soulsplit] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/544195488447201300.png?v=1 deflectmelee] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/544195487926845462.png?v=1 deflectmage] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/544195488317046812.png?v=1 deflectrange] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1137809111178813471.png?v=1 deflectnecromancy]
⬥ [https://youtu.be/Ft48eKVdNVQ Soul Split flicking Arch Glacor] ⬥ [https://youtu.be/olxSzdM1gDs Soul Split flicking Raksha]

[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

Introduction

Note: a Table of Contents can be found in the pinned messages.

​

Runescape has 3 different combat modes: revolution (revo), revolution++ (revo++) and full manual (FM).

This guide aims to cover what these different game modes are, what a player just starting out might want to use, and how to transition to using full manual.

​

Combat modes can be configured by going to Esc > Gameplay Settings > Combat & Action Bar > Combat Mode.

​

Related guides

For further information and reading, you can refer to the following resources.

Quick Navigation Links
Links to related guides and resources for more info about PvM and DPS. Use the Community help (external Discord) if you want to ask any questions, or post clips/videos for review and feedback.
Getting Started
⬥ [[PvME/Learning to boss/Bossing Path|Bossing Path]] ⬥ [[PvME/Getting started/Interface Guide|Interface Guide]] ⬥ [[PvME/Learning to boss/Learning PvM|Learning PvM]]
Damage guides
⬥ [[PvME/Damage rotations/Damage rotations FAQ|DPM Advice Faq]] ⬥ [[PvME/Damage rotations/Magic damage guide|DPM Advice Mage]] ⬥ [[PvME/Damage rotations/Melee damage guide|DPM Advice Melee]] ⬥ [[PvME/Damage rotations/Necromancy damage guide|DPM Advice Necro]] ⬥ [[PvME/Damage rotations/Ranged damage guide|DPM Advice Range]]
Community help (external Discord)
⬥ [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/656898197561802760 PvM help (external Discord)] ⬥ [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1021152606455873686 PvM help forums (external Discord)] ⬥ [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/1019648841965916220 VOD reviews (external Discord)]

​

Revolution (Revo)

Note: For a list of of revo/revo++bars, see !revo, !revo++ ‎and !aoe.

⬥ Revolution lets the game automatically activate abilities on your ability bar in sequential order (based on adrenaline and cooldowns).

⬥ Revo can be configured to activate any combination of:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Basic abilities

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Threshold abilities

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Enhanced abilities

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Ultimate abilities

⬥ If configured to also use enhanced and ultimate abilities for you, it is referred to as revo++.

⬥ Remember, you can still provide user input to override revo/revo++ when you want.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• This may be easier with ability queueing on.

​

Is Revolution Good?

⬥ It gives up some control over using your basics but also means less user input is required.

⬥ Some reasons revo can helpful include:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• You're just getting into PvM

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Combat seems to have too much to focus on

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• You want the game to use basics but still have control over stronger abilities.

⬥ For most combat situations, you can get away with using Revo

⬥ There are helpful guides and ability bar setups that can make it work.

​

Is Revolution++ Good?

⬥ Revo++ makes the game far more AFK, by reducing user input significantly.

⬥ This comes at the cost of flexibility and adaptability to different combat situations.

⬥ Places where Revo++ is useful:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• AFK tasks like Slayer [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896049548066857.png?v=1 slayer]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Special Revo++ bars specifically designed for a particular boss

⬥ Ideally avoid Revo++ outside the above scenarios → prefer normal Revo everywhere else.

​

Full Manual

What Is Full Manual

⬥ In full manual, you must use every ability you want yourself - the game activates nothing for you.

⬥ If no inputs are given, full manual will only use auto attacks.

⬥ It has a higher skill floor, but also rewards the player for the effort they put into it.

​

Is Full Manual Required?

⬥ Full manual is not required to play or enjoy the game, but progressively harder content will benefit from using it.

⬥ It is recommended to learn full manual at some point.

⬥ Full manual offers more control over what you use:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• You can slow down or burst your DPS at important times in a boss fight

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• You can save abilities for specific scenarios (e.g. stuns for when you need them, or AoE abilities

​

Revo vs. Full Manual - Why You Should Switch!

In this section, we cover some reasons why full manual is preferable. Afterwards, in How to Switch to Full Manual, we discuss how you can progress there.

​

Ultimate Abilities

⬥ You should use ultimates manually even if using Revo (except for stuff like full AFK slayer, etc.)

⬥ Good Revo bars will have stronger abilities near the front of the bar so they get used more frequently.

⬥ This is good for general usage but detrimental for damage-boosting ultimates.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• e.g. Sunshine [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/994921119381463070.png?v=1 sunshine] / Death's Swiftness [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/994921434633744455.png?v=1 deathsswift] / Berserk [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535532854004678657.png?v=1 zerk] / Living Death [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1159434908486357072.png?v=1 livingdeath]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Stronger abilities will likely be on cooldown at the when you use your ultimate, due to being at the front of the revo bar.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Some of the best abilities are bleeds which will be near the front of the revo bar, but bleeds are NOT boosted by damage boosting ultimates.

⬥ Whereas if you use full manual, you have full control:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Strong abilities can be saved until you are within the ultimate to get more out of them.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Use of bleeds can be reduced/avoided in damage boosting ultimates since you can just choose to not press them.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• You can even choose the right time to use your ultimate (e.g. don't use it before the boss becomes immune, etc.)

​

⬥ The clip below will demonstrate how Revo can make someone use bad abilities in a damage-boosting ultimate. See what abilities were used right after Sunshine [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/994921119381463070.png?v=1 sunshine]:

[https://img.pvme.io/images/iwArsuMX77.mp4 Source media]

⬥ If using full manual instead, they could have better planned out what abilities to use before using [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/994921119381463070.png?v=1 sunshine]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• They could have made sure the good abilities like Dragon Breath [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535533833391702017.png?v=1 dbreath] are off cooldown and ready immediately after [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/994921119381463070.png?v=1 sunshine], by using other abilities to build adrenaline like Combust [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1478063107908702482.png?v=1 combust] or the Basic Attack [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1478063104146411713.png?v=1 magicbasic].

​

Boss Mechanics

As you progress in PvM and face tougher and tougher bosses, you will encounter bosses with mechanics where revolution could greatly hinder your combat ability. Here are a few scenarios where Revo could cause more harm than good:

​

⬥ Araxxor [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513213019543699466.png?v=1 Araxxi]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• During his web shield, players must manually input to stop attacking, otherwise all damage dealt gets reflected onto the player, potentially killing them.

⬥ Vorago [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/572867742613635082.png?v=1 vorago]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• During his reflect mechanic, similar to Araxxor, players must manually stop attacking to prevent killing themselves or another person via reflect damage.

⬥ Telos [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513212949033123840.png?v=1 Telos]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• For his "Hold Still, Invader" attack, you Anticipate [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541306475151390.png?v=1 anti] and use Resonance [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541258844635148.png?v=1 res]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• This requires somewhat precise timing and there's a chance Revolution activates an ability while you are waiting to Resonance [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541258844635148.png?v=1 res], triggering the global cooldown which can mess up the timing.

⬥ Kalphite King [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513212971409866765.png?v=1 KalphiteKing]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• During his 'Green' attack, a player needs to provoke [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541259465392143.png?v=1 voke] the boss and use either Devotion [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513190158728953857.png?v=1 devo] or Resonance [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541258844635148.png?v=1 res] to avoid dying

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• If Revolution uses something else and delays the defensives, it might kill them.

⬥ Nex [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513213159071547395.png?v=1 Nex]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Any attacks during her 'Blood Siphon' will heal Nex rather than hurt her, requiring manual input to prevent Revolution from attacking her.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• During Blood Phase, Nex heals from bleeds, requiring manual input to avoid using bleeds.

⬥ Helwyr [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/513213019635843100.png?v=1 Helwyr]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• A common way to deal with his 'You Will Bleed!' swipe attack is to Resonance [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541258844635148.png?v=1 res] it to heal some HP.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• This needs somewhat precise timing and there's a chance that Revolution activates an ability while you are waiting to Resonance [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541258844635148.png?v=1 res], triggering the global cooldown which can mess up the timing.

⬥ Arch-Glacor [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/891948878583189514.png?v=1 archglacor]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• During his 'Arms' mechanic, players must quickly deal damage on one of his arms to break free.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Revolution might waste a strong ability on the boss (who is immune at this point) before you switch to target his arms, lowering your DPS output.

⬥ Zamorak [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/994914159969976440.png?v=1 zamorak]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• During his Infernal Tomb mechanic, players must Anticipate [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541306475151390.png?v=1 anti] and then stun on a specific tick.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Missing this stun could cost you the kill or force you to use Immortality [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/535541258538582017.png?v=1 immort] at higher enrages.

​

Revo with (Mostly) Manual Inputs

⬥ There is not much difference between using Full Manual without Revolution, vs. Full Manual with Revolution as a backup.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• The main difference is it ensures you don't suddenly use an ability that you didn't intend to.

​

How to Switch from Revolution to Full Manual

Learning full manual can take time - this is normal. However, just like with any other game, its not unreasonable to expect players to pick up the required skill over time.

Step by Step

⬥ Set good keybinds.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• It is very important that your keybinds are comfortable to reach and make sense to you.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• It is up to you to decide what works best for you.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• See the Action Bars and Keybinds sections in [[PvME/Getting started/Interface Guide|Interface Guide]] for some ideas.

​

⬥ Practice the keybinds.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• You need to be able to use your keybinds effectively - this means committing them to muscle memory.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Your goal is to not need to think about what keybind does what ability - you should know what ability you want to do, and the muscle memory should do the rest for you.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• It is normal for this to take some time, but trust the process!

​

⬥ Choose - gradual transition, or full sending it.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Some players find it easier to start to keep Revo on for backup, but focus on using more manual inputs until they can turn off Revo entirely.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Others may just jump in and turn off Revo, and practice until they can effectively use their binds, and not lose time trying to use abilities.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• It is up to you to decide what works best for you.

​

⬥ Focused practice

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• When practicing keybinds, make sure the focus is practicing keybinds.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• This means you shouldn't try to learn too many other things at the same time, such as prayer flicking or new boss mechanics, etc.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Get used to full manual doing PvM you're already familiar with.

​

⬥ Good places to practice keybinds:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Combat Dummies [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/656844963522281473.png?v=1 dummy] - to initially learn your keybinds.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Full manual slayer - makes you think about prioritising abilities and using AoEs properly.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• GWD2 - relatively easy bosses with few mechanics and high health to practice rotations on (plus decent [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/698816156961603654.png?v=1 coins] profit!)

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Arch-Glacor [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/891948878583189514.png?v=1 archglacor] - toggleable mechanics for a customised fight to practice movement, defensives, and DPS checks.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Check out [[PvME/Learning to boss/Bossing Path|Bossing Path]] for more ideas.

​

Keybinds Guide

⬥ As a reference, check out this very well thought out guide to setting up your keybinds that can help you plan your own keybinds.

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zn_y-_2giZg https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zn_y-_2giZg]

​

[[PvME|PvME guide index]]

Introduction

Combat is a key pillar of the game and can be overwhelming at times - it need not be this way! The aim of this guide is to help you get up and running with some ideas on how to train your levels whilst being fully immersed into the world of RuneScape.

​

We will cover in this guide:

⬥ Some key tips before you start

⬥ Early game combat quests to help you gain some levels whilst being immersed in the lore

⬥ Some training suggestions (these are not mandatory)

⬥ An introduction to War's Retreat and some further quest information relating to combat

Some key tips before you start

⬥ Hit chance i.e. your damage scaling when attacking monsters can be viewed as a percentage on the monster's HP bar. The higher the number, the greater your damage.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Wearing "off-style" armour e.g. a melee weapon with magic armour severely impacts your hit chance in a negative manner! Be sure to match your armour combat style with your weapon combat style.

⬥ Attack [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689509250472476758.png?v=1 attack] affects melee accuracy and its level is what determines what melee weapons you can equip. Strength [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689509250879324165.png?v=1 strength] determines your damage dealt with melee weapons.

⬥ The best defence is a good offence: weapon upgrades take precedence over armour upgrades!

⬥ You will level quickly in the early levels - if you feel like you can survive without issues, skip an armour upgrade and save your gold for the following one

⬥ When using Magic [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689504724159823906.png?v=1 magic] you should regularly upgrade your auto-cast to the highest available spell tier. You can find out a spell's damage level cap by checking its tooltip.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• For example: Air strike's damage cap is at level 16 - you can upgrade to Air bolt at level 17.

⬥ If you need help, don't struggle in silence! You can ask questions in the help channels of:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• The official Runescape Discord [https://discord.com/invite/rs invite link (external Discord)] [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/723915055976153138 Affiliates (external Discord)]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• The PvM Encyclopedia [https://discord.gg/invite/pvme invite link (external Discord)] [https://discord.com/channels/534508796639182860/656898197561802760 PvM help (external Discord)]

Early Combat

Quests can be a great way to get the early levels in any skill, including combat [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896050370281523.png?v=1 combat] skills

​

Some initial quests we highly recommend are the following:

​

⬥ These set you up to more easily manage other early quest fights:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• [https://runescape.wiki/w/Waterfall_Quest Waterfall quest] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689509250879324165.png?v=1 strength] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689509250472476758.png?v=1 attack]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• [https://runescape.wiki/w/Merlin%27s_Crystal Merlin's crystal] → [https://runescape.wiki/w/Holy_Grail Holy grail] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689509250979987525.png?v=1 defence] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1005450651347730533.png?v=1 prayer]

​

⬥ For [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1148995625896120460.png?v=1 necromancy]:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• [https://runescape.wiki/w/Necromancy! Necromancy! (tutorial quest)]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Gather 400 souls to lvl20; fragile mementos are recommended

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• At level 20 & 24: [https://runescape.wiki/w/Kili_Row Kili row] and [https://runescape.wiki/w/Rune_Mythos Rune Mythos] quests

​

⬥ These quests require fighting and introduce you to combat - you'll be rewarded for your efforts with [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896050370281523.png?v=1 combat] xp:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎(the skill icons indicate where we think you should spend that xp)

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• [https://runescape.wiki/w/Vampyre_Slayer Vampyre Slayer] - Use the xp reward on [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689504724159823906.png?v=1 magic] or [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/580168050121113623.png?v=1 range]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• [https://runescape.wiki/w/Witch's_House Witch's House] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689509250887712902.png?v=1 constitution]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• [https://runescape.wiki/w/Fight_Arena Fight Arena] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689509250472476758.png?v=1 attack] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1039864807920250900.png?v=1 thieving]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ Use Halberd or [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/580168050121113623.png?v=1 range] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689504724159823906.png?v=1 magic] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1148995625896120460.png?v=1 necromancy] to safespot the boss fight

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• [https://runescape.wiki/w/The_Grand_Tree/Quick_guide Grand Tree] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896050370281523.png?v=1 combat] lamp

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ Use Halberd or [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/580168050121113623.png?v=1 range] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689504724159823906.png?v=1 magic] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1148995625896120460.png?v=1 necromancy] to safespot the boss fight

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• [https://runescape.wiki/w/Tree_Gnome_Village Tree gnome village] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689509250472476758.png?v=1 attack]

​

⬥ The quest and miniquest below offer a reward which will greatly enhance your damage against undead creatures:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎(we recommend having level 50 [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896050370281523.png?v=1 combat] skills and gear)

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• [https://runescape.wiki/w/Haunted_Mine Haunted Mine]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• [https://runescape.wiki/w/Lair_of_Tarn_Razorlor_(miniquest) Miniquest: Lair of Tarn Razorlor]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎⬩ Yields: salve amulet(e) [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797899945730244648.png?v=1 salveamulet]

Note: This amulet gives +20% accuracy and damage against [https://runescape.wiki/w/Salve_amulet_(e) Undead] creatures

​

⬥ The quest below unlocks the [https://runescape.wiki/w/Ancient_Magicks ancient spellbook] and therefore [https://runescape.wiki/w/Vampyrism Vampyrism] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1494069423047442573.png?v=1 vampyrismaspect], providing a powerful early sustain unlock:

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• [https://runescape.wiki/w/Desert_Treasure Desert Treasure]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Also requires level 69 magic [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689504724159823906.png?v=1 magic] to cast, which can be boosted using potions

​

Combat [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896050370281523.png?v=1 combat] Training

If questing isn't your cup of tea - getting stuck into killing some monsters might be more your style:

​

⬥ Combat levelling focuses on killing monsters for xp

⬥ Upgrade your weapons to a higher tier when you can!

⬥ Include area-of-effect (AoE) abilities as they become available. Check ability tooltips.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Ranged [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/580168050121113623.png?v=1 range]: [https://runescape.wiki/w/Chinchompa chinchompas] turn non-AoE abilities into AoE attacks within 1 tile of the target

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Melee [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1096130867279171706.png?v=1 melee]: [https://runescape.wiki/w/Halberd halberds] gives a longer range on AoE attacks

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Magic [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689504724159823906.png?v=1 magic]: [https://runescape.wiki/w/Ancient_Magicks ancient spellbook] gives AoE basic attacks, but requires the [https://runescape.wiki/w/Desert_Treasure Desert Treasure] quest

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Necromancy [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1148995625896120460.png?v=1 necromancy]: AoE tools are largely locked behind levels and [https://runescape.wiki/w/Well_of_Souls Well of Souls] upgrades

​

We also have some pre-created ability bars and gear progression suggestions to help you slay these monsters. You can check them out here:

⬥ Early [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689504724159823906.png?v=1 magic] upgrade order & ability bars:[[PvME/Combat foundations/Early Magic Upgrades|Early Magic Upgrades]]

⬥ Early [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1096130867279171706.png?v=1 melee] upgrade order & ability bars: [[PvME/Combat foundations/Early Melee Upgrades|Early Melee Upgrades]]

⬥ Early [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/580168050121113623.png?v=1 range] upgrade order & ability bars: [[PvME/Combat foundations/Early Ranged Upgrades|Early Ranged Upgrades]]

⬥ Early [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1148995625896120460.png?v=1 necromancy] upgrade order, talent tree & ability bars:[[PvME/Combat foundations/Early Necromancy Upgrades|Early Necromancy Upgrades]]

Some methods you can try out:

Level 1-30:

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Ghostly_troll_bruiser Ghostly Trolls] in City of Um cave

⬥ Monsters in [https://runescape.wiki/w/Lumbridge_Catacombs#Monsters Lumbridge Catacombs] (req. [https://runescape.wiki/w/The_Blood_Pact/Quick_guide Blood Pact])

⬥ Trolls in the [https://runescape.wiki/w/Burthorpe_Troll_Cave Burthorpe Troll Cave]

​

Level 30-50/60:

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Bandit_(Kharidian_Desert_Bandit_Camp) Bandits] in the Bandit Camp bar

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Wear any piece of Saradomin or Zamorak equipment to make them continuously aggressive

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Fetid_zombie Fetid Zombies] ([https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797899945730244648.png?v=1 salveamulet] works)

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Sanguine_crawler Sanguine Crawlers] using upgraded [https://runescape.wiki/w/Havensilver_weapons Havensilver weapons] (req. [https://runescape.wiki/w/Visions_of_Havenhythe Visions of Havenhythe])

​

Level 50/60-80:

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Abyss/Combat_training The Abyss Monsters] (req. [https://runescape.wiki/w/Enter_the_Abyss_(miniquest)/Quick_guide Enter the Abyss miniquest])

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Bound_skeleton Bound Skeletons] ([https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797899945730244648.png?v=1 salveamulet] works)

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Flesh-hatcher_Mhekarnahz Flesh-hatcher Mhekarnahz]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• Boss, recommended to start from level 60 [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/580168050121113623.png?v=1 ranged] or level 70 [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1096130867279171706.png?v=1 melee] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/689504724159823906.png?v=1 magic] / [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1148995625896120460.png?v=1 necromancy]

​

At any point you may also opt to try [https://runescape.wiki/w/Slayer_assignment Slayer Assignments] for the sake of variety or to familiarise yourself with different monsters throughout the game world

​

War's Retreat & Bossing

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/War%27s_Retreat War's Retreat] is a PvM hub that can be accessed at [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896050370281523.png?v=1 combat] Level 60 or with a Total Level of 1000 north of Draynor lodestone

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• This place can serve as a free, unlimited place to teleport to for easy bank access, restoring prayer and more as you increase your boss kill count

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• To unlock the teleport, it is recommended to kill 10 lower level bosses such as [https://runescape.wiki/w/Ivar,_King_of_Bones Ivar, King of Bones], [https://runescape.wiki/w/King_Black_Dragon King Black Dragon], or [https://runescape.wiki/w/Giant_mole Giant Mole]

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• For more info on bossing see [[PvME/Learning to boss/Bossing Path|Bossing Path]]

​

⬥ [https://runescape.wiki/w/Soul_Reaper Reaper tasks] are a PvM activity that can be accessed at [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896050370281523.png?v=1 combat] Level 50 with 45 Slayer [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896049548066857.png?v=1 slayer] by talking to Death, north of Draynor lodestone

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• You earn Reaper points [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/704657943194501140.png?v=1 reaperpoints] to spend on rewards by killing bosses in a quantity that Death assigns you. You will only be given bosses that you have the levels/unlocks to access.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• You will also gain Slayer [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/797896049548066857.png?v=1 slayer] experience for completing the task

Quests

⬥ For a list of quests with useful PvM unlocks, see Quest Unlocks in [[PvME/Gear upgrades/Permanent Unlocks|Permanent Unlocks]]

⬥ One of the first useful unlocks to aim for is the tier 3 [https://runescape.wiki/w/Infernal_Puzzle_Box Infernal Puzzle Box] [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/994189299681607800.png?v=1 infernalpuzzlebox], which prevents your adrenaline from draining when outside of combat

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• You can find the box in [https://runescape.wiki/w/The_Zamorakian_Undercity#Getting_there The Zamorakian Undercity] specifically [https://runescape.wiki/w/Infernal_Puzzle_Box#mapFullscreen here]. Completing the [https://runescape.wiki/w/Daughter_of_Chaos/Quick_guide Daughter of Chaos] quest (40 Archaeology [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/941211288665739274.png?v=1 archaeology] and 40 Divination [https://cdn.discordapp.com/emojis/1042453694735712286.png?v=1 divination]) unlocks tier 2.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎• To unlock tier 3, complete the [https://runescape.wiki/w/Civil_War_I_(miniquest)/Quick_guide Civil War I] miniquest, and the [https://runescape.wiki/w/Gross_Misconduct Gross Misconduct achievement]

⬥ Two quests also worth mentioning are [https://runescape.wiki/w/The_Temple_at_Senntisten/Quick_guide The Temple at Senntisten] and [https://runescape.wiki/w/Plague%27s_End/Quick_guide Plague's End]. The first unlocks curses, which are basically stronger prayers. The second unlocks better overloads and combination potions.

⬥ Note that quests are more rewarding the sooner you do them, due to how level XP scaling works

Quest XP Rewards
Full list of experience given in specific skills from [https://runescape.wiki/w/Quests/Experience_rewards quest rewards]

​
